8.4 Observations and Mechanistic Hypotheses

C1: the finite maximum of \(C_V\).

At \(N=2000\), numerical maximization of the exact discrete sum gives \(\gamma \simeq 1.256885\) and \(C_V\simeq 6.919812\). At one, \(C_V=5.484118\), whereas the continuous approximation gives \(4.814477\). This is a property of the chosen statistical family. It neither locates an empirical network transition nor follows by treating the continuous formula as a discrete identity.

C2: large nominal bases do not determine the fitted exponent.

The initial Qwen text fits are \(1.028374\) (0.5B), \(0.772033\) (3B) and \(0.996695\) (7B). This non-monotonic sequence is not explained by a candidate depending only on shared \(\theta \) and evaluation length. For \(T=2000\) and \(\theta =10^6\), the stated Padé expression gives approximately \(0.997\). The initial Llama-3 text fit is \(1.045476\). These comparisons are tests of a proposed predictor, not confirmations from the configuration alone.

Substituting \(\widehat\gamma =.772033\) into the proposed inverse gives

\[ \theta _{\rm eff}^{\star }=\frac{T\sqrt2(1+\widehat\gamma )}{2(1-\widehat\gamma )}\simeq 11{,}000. \]

This is a coordinate of the Padé model, not a recovered physical RoPE base. The Qwen-3B random fit is about \(.964\), so its corpus contrast is about \(+.192\). That observation does not prove intact geometry, absent induction heads, or a mechanism caused by two shared KV heads. Such alternatives require controlled activation or weight interventions. Likewise, large \(\theta \) alone does not count active rotary planes: the actual rotary dimension and phase threshold enter the integer count.

GQA and the proposed pressure analogy.

The ratio of query to KV heads may motivate an architectural hypothesis about shared representations. The present corpus contrast does not identify a pressure, confinement law or training threshold. A matched GQA intervention, with fixed data, distance support and loading precision, would be needed to test that hypothesis.

C3: corpus contrast is descriptive.

Define \(\Delta \gamma =\widehat\gamma _{\rm random}-\widehat\gamma _{\rm text}\). Positive, negative and near-zero contrasts all occur. Six representative pairs appear in Figure 8; the evidence manifest contains 34 available pairs. Each displayed pair is refitted on the intersection of its saved fitting grids. Matching distances does not establish identical tokenizers, prompts, seeds, precision or acquisition runs. A positive sign is not a sufficient detector of sliding-window attention, and a negative sign is not a sufficient detector of GQA or induction heads. No accuracy estimate for such a classifier is established here.

🖼️ Figure 8

Six corpus contrasts recomputed from saved means on a common within-pair grid. Falcon uses 30–1000; the other five pairs use 30–2000. The two formerly absent random-corpus points have saved data: Pythia-70M gives \(+0.422912\) and Qwen2.5-7B gives \(-0.169680\). The bars are point estimates, without an inferred mechanism or an uncomputed confidence interval.

C4: quantization and acquisition checks.

The initial Llama-2 text record contains \(\widehat\gamma =.287057\). Comparing that number with a different platform record cannot isolate a 4-bit effect: corpus, fitting range, implementation and precision must be matched, and the Kaggle metadata discussed above are incomplete. The proposed inverse also has a strict domain: \(\widehat\gamma =1\) is singular and \(\widehat\gamma {\gt}1\) yields a negative value for positive \(T\). It is not a generally valid physical-base estimator for fp16 models. A controlled precision sweep remains the appropriate experiment.

C5: ALiBi and finite-range power-law fits.

BLOOM-7b1 has a text exponent \(1.217824\) with \(R^2=.997330\); the initial random estimate is approximately \(.882\). These fits describe sampled distances, not an infinite tail. A mixture of content scores and positional biases need not have the same functional form as its bias alone. Larger-distance data and held-out comparison of competing models are required to distinguish power, exponential and mixed tails. The MaxEnt theorem identifies an optimizer under a prescribed moment constraint; it does not demonstrate that training imposes that constraint or that a power law is a universal attractor.

This restriction changes the random estimate of Pythia-2.8B from \(.551\) on its longer recorded range to \(.790851\) on 30–100, producing \(\Delta \gamma =+.116690\). Comparing \(.551\) with the three-point text estimate would mix supports.

Connection to induction-head dynamics.

Induction-head research olsson2022induction motivates testing copy-specific activation patterns and their causal contribution during training. The proposed connection remains a testable mechanism hypothesis.

On the currently saved 30–1000 aggregates, the pure log-log fit gives \(R^2=.989728\) for text and \(.967807\) for random. An unconstrained log-linear mixed fit on those same points gives negative \(\lambda \) in both corpora, and therefore does not reproduce the positive-cutoff summary above. 8.5 Evidence and replay protocol

The archived October atlas supplies 25 measurements among 42 historical identifiers. We recomputed the binning, regression and bootstrap from the saved NumPy profiles, and matched each row to its successful checkpoint record. The maximum exponent discrepancy was below \(3\times 10^{-15}\); the maximum interval-endpoint discrepancy was below \(1.4\times 10^{-9}\). The latter reflects storage of sequence profiles in 32-bit floats. These checks reproduce computations on saved data; they do not rerun the model or certify that its implementation was correct.

The source protocol uses text from the recorded pile-10k snapshot, selecting documents long enough for the model’s tokenizer and context, and taking their first \(T\) tokens. This does not guarantee identical documents or token sequences across models. All 25 successful records report zero non-finite attention fraction. That field is a recorded instrument check, not independently reconstructed full attention tensors. Four job records identify an immutable model revision in their own metadata; the others use mutable names or local paths. The hashes of saved profiles do not repair that limitation.

Seventeen historical models have no corresponding October measurement in this reconstruction. They are missing observations, not failures with zero exponent, and are excluded from the following denominators. The table also mixes 15 contexts of 2048 and 10 of 1024, different precisions and model-specific tokenizers. Its rows should not be treated as a controlled intervention on architecture.

One model, several instruments.

Pythia-2.8B illustrates the scale of protocol dependence: E4 text gives \(0.674162\) on three distances; E4 random gives about \(0.551\) on its longer range and \(0.790851\) on the matched short support; QL at \(T=2048\) gives \(0.866809\); the field fit is about \(0.969\), its mean of cell fits about \(1.309\), and the layer-summary record about \(1.327\). These are distinct estimands and records. In particular an E4 curve samples different rows and lengths: it is not a probability vector on distances. Substituting its slope into \(p_g(d)\) constructs a new family member. Its entropy and quantiles must not be exported as measured attention mass or KV retention.

Descriptive controls in the fixed-query panel.

The eight Pythia QL point estimates decrease strictly with size: \(1.244,1.233,1.174,1.073,0.984,0.974,0.930,0.867\) (Spearman \(-1\)). At their shared nominal \(\theta =10000,T=2048\), the candidate is constant (\(0.747006\)). This is a descriptive trend in saved fits; overlapping intervals, one checkpoint per size, changing architecture and missing immutable revisions limit causal attribution to scale. GPT-2 variants, which use learned absolute positions, span about \(0.791\)–\(0.899\) and overlap the RoPE panel. A fitted distance slope therefore does not uniquely identify RoPE. These controls motivate matched prospective measurements.

Checkpoint names and identity.

The initial source JSONs identify google/gemma-2-9b-it, codellama/CodeLlama-13b-Instruct-hf and microsoft/phi-3-mini-4k-instruct; abbreviated labels such as “Gemma-2-9B” do not denote verified base checkpoints. The QL table names the same variants. Matching repository names does not establish identical weight revisions, and the separate 42-row legacy atlas must not be confused with the 21-row initial E4 panel. Historical/QL agreement remains a comparison of archived identifiers with incomplete execution provenance.

8.7 Historical agreement and the Padé comparison

The historical text exponent lies inside the October bootstrap interval for one of 25 models. Spearman correlation between historical and QL exponents is \(0.269\). The 19 rows with a stored Padé value give Spearman correlation \(-0.445\) against the QL exponent. Ties in the Padé values receive average ranks. These are descriptive calculations, not corrected significance tests or prospective predictive evaluations.

9 Diagnostic Workflow and Instrument Controls

A fitted exponent describes the combination of an attention mechanism and a measurement protocol. The first diagnostic question is whether that protocol produces a slope on a null distribution. A high in-sample \(R^2\) cannot answer that question: the uniform control below has \(R^2=0.988452\) on the main E4 grid. The earlier speed claims and universal diagnostic thresholds are not established by this manuscript. The command examples elsewhere are historical interfaces.

9.1 Variable-length E4 has a nonzero uniform null

Groups 1–2 in Appendix K generalize this control to weighted probes and prove strict bounds and monotonicity for affine exposure.

The available E4 extractor sets the sequence length to \(n(d)=d+50\), reads the last query \(i=d+49\), and samples key \(j=49\). Thus it changes the query, available context and row normalizer with distance while holding the key index fixed. For uniform causal attention, including the query’s own key,

\begin{equation} A_0(d)=\frac{1}{d+50},\qquad \widehat\gamma _0= \frac{\sum _k(x_k-\bar x)(\log (d_k+50)-\overline{\log (d+50)})}{\sum _k(x_k-\bar x)^2},\quad x_k=\log d_k. \tag {46} \end{equation}
47

This is an OLS slope caused by the instrument; it does not require trained weights, positional encoding or token semantics. Its local log slope is \(d/(d+50)\), which rises with distance. The short/long slope contrast can therefore occur under a uniform null too.

These values were checked both analytically and by passing synthetic causal attention tensors through the saved E4 extraction and fitting functions. No language model was run. For the mixture \((1-s)U_n+s\delta _0\), with constant \(s{\lt}1\) and \(U_n\) uniform on all \(n=d+50\) eligible keys, off-sink entries are \((1-s)/(d+50)\) and the slope is unchanged. If instead key zero receives exactly \(s\) and the other \(n-1\) keys share \(1-s\), entries are \((1-s)/(d+49)\): the seven-point null is \(0.785491\), rather than \(0.782582\). A context-dependent sink mass introduces another dependence. Failed heads, masks and nonfinite-value exclusions require correspondingly matched controls.

The configuration value \(\gamma _P(10^4,2000)=0.752201\) lies close to this instrumental slope, but closeness alone neither proves nor quantifies the fraction of an empirical fit caused by the confound. The former accuracy comparison cannot identify rotary geometry as the cause. Likewise, weak responses to steering or an exponent near \(0.75\) at initialization do not independently establish a learned geometric law.

9.2 Fixed queries distinguish QL from diagonal averaging

The October QL implementation uses the same query set \(Q=\{ T-\lfloor T/4\rfloor ,\ldots ,T-1\} \) at every fitted distance. Under uniform causal attention its profile is

\[ A_{0,\mathrm{QL}}(d)=|Q|^{-1}\sum _{i\in Q}\frac{1}{i+1}, \qquad 16\le d\le T/2, \]

which is constant in \(d\). In contrast, the ALL profile averages over queries \(i\ge d\) and has null

\[ A_{0,\mathrm{ALL}}(d)=\frac{1}{T-d}\sum _{i=d}^{T-1}\frac{1}{i+1}. \]

Running the actual QL accumulator and logarithmic-bin fitter on synthetic matrices gives \(|\widehat\gamma _0|{\lt}10^{-10}\) at \(T=1024\) and \(2048\), both with and without an added sink of mass \(0.2\). For ALL including key zero but without additional sink mass, the slopes are \(0.317033\) at \(T=1024\) and \(0.298064\) at \(T=2048\). The two numbers index context lengths, not the presence versus absence of a sink. These numbers use 16 bins over \([16,T/2]\); other ranges or weighting rules produce other ALL slopes. They must not be attributed to QL.

The full stored QL profile reaches \(d=3T/4\). At that last endpoint one query does sample key zero, contrary to a comment in the instrument. The fitted range \([16,T/2]\) excludes that endpoint and all key-zero terms. This boundary distinction is part of the instrument audit, not a correction to the 25 saved QL fits. A flat synthetic control verifies the reduction on that null; it does not certify real-model acquisition, masking, precision or provenance.

9.3 Report the observable and its matched control

For the same distances, exclusions and regression weights, linearity of OLS gives

\begin{equation} \widehat\gamma _{\mathrm{excess}} =\widehat\gamma -\widehat\gamma _0 =-\operatorname {slope}_{\log d}\log \! \left(\frac{A(d)}{A_0(d)}\right). \tag {47} \end{equation}
48

The reproducibility package records this diagnostic for all 21 initial-panel rows, retaining each original slope, grid and source. It assumes the recorded row was acquired with the declared \(d+50\) procedure; incomplete provenance is not repaired by that assumption. The excess slope is not automatically a causal or learned exponent, and fitting a ratio does not turn it into a normalized probability distribution. Corpus comparisons must also use common within-pair supports.

A prospective measurement should fix context length and query positions, state whether self and sink keys are excluded, and archive per-sequence profiles, exclusions, model/tokenizer revisions, attention implementation, precision, corpus and seed. Uniform causal, uniform-plus-sink, randomized weights and shuffled-token controls answer different questions. Only the first two synthetic controls are executed in this revision. Alternative families should be compared on held-out sequences under the same observation and loss conventions. Resample sequences, not individual distances, for uncertainty when sequence-level records exist.

9.4 Derived family quantities and inverse coordinates

For a declared finite power-law family, compute \(Z_N\), entropy, Fisher information and \(C_V\) by finite sums. These quantities describe that family; they do not establish model sensitivity to context changes. \(1/\gamma \) is a formal temperature only when nonzero, and positive-temperature interpretation requires \(\gamma {\gt}0\). The intervals around \(0.95\) and \(1.05\) were heuristic labels, not validated architecture classifiers.

The correct inverse of the rational candidate at fixed \(T{\gt}0\) is

\begin{equation} \theta _{\rm inv}(g,T)=\frac{T\sqrt2(1+g)}{2(1-g)}, \qquad -1{\lt}g{\lt}1. \tag {48} \end{equation}
49

It is a positive algebraic coordinate on that domain. It does not recover a physical training base from an observed slope. The former expression \(T\sqrt2/(1-g)\) is the inverse of a linear approximation; substituting \(g=\gamma _P(\theta ,T)\) gives \(\theta +T/\sqrt2\), not \(\theta \). Exponents at or above one cannot be inverted into a positive base by the candidate.

9.5 Divergence from a declared reference

For positive normalized reference \(q\) and observed probability \(p\) on the same support, a descriptive discrepancy is

\begin{equation} \mathrm{KL}_{\rm grammar}=\sum _d p(d)\log \frac{p(d)}{q(d)}, \qquad q(d)=d^{-g}/\sum _{r\in \mathcal D}r^{-g}. \tag {49} \end{equation}
50

The available diagnostic script normalizes sparse sampled distances with equal point weights, rather than reconstructing all token distances or bin masses. Its KL therefore refers to that sampled support. Neither a small KL nor the old cutoff \(0.05\) identifies a positional circuit, attention sink or induction head. Circuit attribution needs functional evidence beyond a residual.

9.6 Reassessment of the four historical cases

LLaMA-2-7B.

The reported \(0.287\) and \(1.026\) slopes are retained as historical records, but the recovered arrays and notes disagree (Section 8). They do not certify a matched fp16/4-bit effect, size invariance or an NTK recommendation. A value above one also lies outside the positive-base inverse domain.

Mistral-7B-v0.1.

The old random/text pair \(0.830/1.061\) is a protocol-specific report. The official configuration declares a 4096-token sliding window; a sequence of at most 2050 tokens does not exclude a key by that window. A direct SWA-mask mechanism therefore cannot explain this short-context contrast. The configuration source is https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1/blob/main/config.json. Architectural and training differences remain possible confounds, and \(\Delta \gamma \) is not a GQA detector.

Qwen2.5-7B.

A fitted value \(0.997\) does not imply purely positional attention. The limiting continuous calculation is \(2000^{0.9}=935.248\), while using \(g=0.997\) gives a different quantile. Neither is a measured token-retention or accuracy result; the discrete values are tabulated below.

Pythia-2.8B.

Its initial text fit uses only distances 30, 50 and 100. The uniform null on that grid is \(0.525737\), and common-support comparison changes the random/text contrast. No long-context safety, stability or optimal cache policy follows from that three-point exponent.

10 Layer Heterogeneity and the Proposed Critical Layer

Layer-resolved profiles, recovery interventions and representation similarity measure different observables. Their agreement should be tested under a common protocol rather than built into the definition of a boundary. This section preserves the original layer reports while separating a proposed configuration formula from measured thresholds.

10.1 A candidate layer coordinate

Definition 10.1 Historical layer-coordinate proposal
#
📕 p. 48📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

For \(\theta {\gt}1\), \(T{\gt}0\), \(N_L\) layers and head dimension \(d_{\rm head}{\gt}0\), define

\begin{equation} L_{\rm pred}=N_L\log _\theta (T/(2\pi )) (d_{\rm head}/64)^{1/\sqrt{12}}. \end{equation}
51

This is the historical configuration proposal previously denoted \(L_{\rm crit}\). Its full-head factor also ignores partial RoPE: Pythia-1B has \(d_{\rm head}=256\) but \(d_{\rm rot}=64\). Replacing one by the other would define a new candidate, not validate the old formula. Its value need not be an integer or lie in \([0,N_L]\); rounding and any clipping must be stated before comparing it to a measured layer index.

Cite: Definition 10.1, p. 48, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

💡 In plain words

\(L_{\rm pred}\) keeps a historical proposal for a layer coordinate as a candidate formula. It uses the full head dimension, although some architectures rotate only part of it.

Scope.

It has not been validated as a layer boundary. It may fall outside the range of layers or fail to be an integer; any rounding or clipping must be declared.

The identity \(\operatorname {sd}(\mathrm{Unif}[0,1])=1/\sqrt{12}\) does not derive the empirical architecture exponent. GPT-2 has learned absolute positions and no RoPE base to substitute in this equation. Its historical layer reports remain observations under another protocol, not evaluations of the RoPE formula.

10.2 A mixture does not have the average exponent

Group 3 in Appendix K proves the local-slope, curvature and global-regression statements for any finite positive mixture of powers.

For positive coefficients and two component profiles, the exact local slope is

\begin{equation} \begin{aligned} A(d)& =a d^{-g_1}+b d^{-g_2},\quad a,b{\gt}0,\\ -\frac{d\log A(d)}{d\log d} & =\frac{a g_1d^{-g_1}+b g_2d^{-g_2}}{a d^{-g_1}+b d^{-g_2}}. \end{aligned} \tag {51} \end{equation}
52

The weights depend on distance unless the component exponents coincide or one component vanishes. A global OLS slope of an averaged attention profile therefore need not equal a layer-fraction-weighted mean of fitted exponents. That equality also fails to account for finite normalizers and failed fits.

The list \(1.35,1.41,1.12,1.10\) for Pythia-70M survives as a rounded manuscript report; its original layer-profile record was not recovered. It must not be identified with the per-head matrix used for P3 in Section 5.6. That matrix gives finite-head layer means \(1.918196,1.663184,1.529207,1.082143\) for L0–L3, with L4–L5 missing; the L1–L3 mean is \(1.424844\), whereas the old list gives \(1.210000\) there. For the old four-entry list, the arithmetic mean is \(1.245\); multiplying by \(4/6\) gives \(0.830\), not \(0.748\). Even the corrected arithmetic is not a derivation of the global slope. The entries marked NaN in layers 4–5 denote unavailable or rejected fits, not an exponent zero or proof of semantic processing. The duplicate reported and predicted values in the old table are not independent validation without the original fitting and parameter-selection record.

10.3 CKA is a separate observation

The companion analysis marin2026coordination was cited for adjacent-layer CKA values near one before a proposed boundary and below \(0.5\) afterwards. Those historical claims are preserved in the audit record. A CKA change can motivate a shared analysis, but does not by itself identify positional versus semantic computation or validate Equation (50). A confirming test must specify the same checkpoint, examples, representations, indexing and threshold selection, and evaluate agreement on held-out observations.

10.4 Training checkpoints and recovery normalization

The saved H3 experiment has eight checkpoints, including step 3000, and uses 50 prompts. Its recovery normalization contains \(\mu _{d=10}-\mu _{\rm baseline}\). A negative denominator reverses the intended direction; one close to zero amplifies numerical variation. A missing or unstable threshold does not imply that a physical layer boundary ceases to exist. The stored threshold outputs and denominators are preserved in Section 8 and in the reproducibility package.

The attention trajectory has nine checkpoints, including 4000 and 64000 but not 3000. These are separate protocols. Its fitted exponent exceeds one at steps 8000 and 16000, not throughout steps 2000–32000. Within the power-law family, a larger positive exponent means steeper decay, not maximally spread attention. Agreement at the final checkpoint does not establish a stable attractor, a formation time for induction heads or an evaporation mechanism. Those interpretations need independent circuit interventions.

11 KV-Cache Compression: Mass Budgets and Recorded Tests

Groups 4 and 6 in Appendix K prove the discrete quantile order and the exact frozen-row truncation identities, including their domains and sharp bounds.

A mass quantile answers a distributional question on a declared support. It does not by itself identify a quality-preserving cache policy. In particular, the variable-length E4 fits have the instrumental confound demonstrated in Section 9.1. The family calculations below remain mathematically valid, while using a fitted model slope as their input requires a matched measurement and evaluation protocol.

11.1 Continuous and discrete windows

Theorem 11.1 Finite continuous mass window
#
📕 p. 50📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

For density proportional to \(d^{-g}\) on \([1,N]\), \(N{\gt}1\), and \(0{\lt}f{\lt}1\), the unique \(f\)-mass quantile is

\begin{equation} D_{f,c}= \begin{cases} [(1-f)+fN^{1-g}]^{1/(1-g)},& g\ne 1,\\ N^f,& g=1. \end{cases} \end{equation}
53

For token distances \(\{ 1,\ldots ,N\} \) with counting measure, the corresponding exact quantile is instead \(D_{f,N}=\min \{ k:\sum _{d=1}^k d^{-g}\ge f\sum _{d=1}^N d^{-g}\} \). For the discrete case \(N\) is an integer. Both quantiles are defined for every finite real \(g\); they do not include a self key at \(d=0\) or a separately modelled attention sink.

Proof: in this note·Covers: not formalized·Cite: Theorem 11.1, p. 50, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

For \(g\ne 1\), dividing \(\int _1^D d^{-g}\, \mathrm{d}d\) by \(\int _1^N d^{-g}\, \mathrm{d}d\) gives \((D^{1-g}-1)/(N^{1-g}-1)\); both integrals contain the factor \(1/(1-g)\). Equating this ratio to \(f\) yields the stated formula. At \(g=1\), the ratio is \(\log D/\log N\). In either case the cumulative density is strictly increasing. On the discrete support, partial sums increase strictly and the smallest index meeting the mass condition is unique.

💡 In plain words

For the continuous density proportional to \(d^{-g}\) on \([1,N]\), integrating and solving for the cumulative mass gives an explicit quantile, with the case \(g=1\) equal to \(N^f\). For integer distances, the exact quantile is the first index whose partial sum reaches the requested fraction. The two quantiles are not interchangeable and neither guarantees accuracy on a KV task.

Formal scope.

The analytic proof is in the paper; this entry does not claim an Isabelle proof of the whole continuous formula or of model performance.

🧪 Lab: Figure 12 live: continuous and integer mass windows

Recompute both quantiles of the finite power family; the integer one is a partial-sum threshold.

For fixed \(g{\lt}1\) and \(f\), the large-\(N\) approximation is \(D_{f,c}\sim Nf^{1/(1-g)}\). It is not uniform as \(g\to 1\) at fixed \(N\). For fixed \(g{\gt}1\) the continuous quantile tends to \((1-f)^{-1/(g-1)}\) as \(N\to \infty \); this is not a geometric-series argument and its accuracy at a particular finite \(N\) must be checked.

11.2 A conditional output bound and actual cache allocation

Let a frozen attention row have weights \(p_j\), values \(v_j\) and removed mass \(0\le \epsilon {\lt}1\). After removing those entries and renormalizing the retained weights, write the retained and removed conditional means as \(o_K,o_R\). For \(\epsilon {\gt}0\), \(o=(1-\epsilon )o_K+\epsilon o_R\), hence

\[ \| o-o_K\| =\epsilon \| o_R-o_K\| \le \epsilon \operatorname {diam}\{ v_j\} \le 2\epsilon \max _j\| v_j\| . \]

The zero-mass case is immediate. The first inequality follows because both conditional means are convex combinations of the values. A subsequent linear projection adds its induced operator norm. This is a frozen-row bound; it does not cover altered hidden states, repeated autoregressive steps or task accuracy after eviction.

For a conventional unexpanded dense cache with \(L\) layers, \(H_{\rm KV}\) key/value heads, head dimension \(d_{\rm head}\) and \(b\) bytes per scalar, physically evicting \(N-W\) tokens saves \(2bLH_{\rm KV}d_{\rm head}(N-W)\) bytes per sequence, before allocator overheads. GQA uses the KV-head count, not the query-head count. Biasing scores or setting weights to zero does not itself reduce a dense allocation. For the old illustrative input \(g=1.046\), \(N=8192\), \(f=0.9\), the continuous window is \(2757.511\), a nominal \(66.34\% \) reduction; the discrete window is \(2537\), a \(69.03\% \) reduction.

These are mass-budget calculations; they neither establish the attention profile at length 8192 nor certify a longer usable context.

11.3 EXP-B2: the windows actually evaluated

The saved two-model record specifies \(N_{\rm full}=2048\), 120 samples and 64 evaluated targets per sample on WikiText-2 test. The available code uses \(W=\operatorname {round}(Nf^{1/(1-g)})\), with a minimum of 64 and a full-window fallback for \(g\ge 1\). Thus the trials at \(W=445\) and \(1482\) test that asymptotic rule, not the exact finite quantile in the theorem.

The two displayed \(+1.4443\) entries are a rounding coincidence: the original Pythia-1B JSON gives \(13.2399089962-11.7955767485=1.4443322477\), while the extended Pythia-160M JSON gives \(23.9412332628-22.4969311427=1.4443021201\). They are distinct saved differences, both reproduced from their recorded PPLs.

The different Pythia-1B and 2.8B deltas in the two panels belong to separate runs and must not be merged. Pythia-14M has \(g=0.685\) yet positive \(\Delta \mathrm{PPL}\) in the extended panel, so the observations do not establish a universal favorable interval such as \([0.65,0.85]\). The 410M entry uses the full window and is not a successful compression trial. The recorded heuristic knee depends on the sampled sweep and its criterion; no optimum or general replacement \(f=0.93\)–\(0.95\) follows from this record.

11.4 Power-law attention allocation: conditional mass budgets

For the discrete family with \(\gamma {\gt}0\), weights decrease with distance. Among sets of a fixed cardinality \(D\), the first \(D\) distances maximise retained family mass. Their mass is

\[ M_N(D)=\frac{\sum _{d=1}^D d^{-\gamma }}{Z_N(\gamma )}. \]

The minimum integer budget attaining mass at least \(f\) is the discrete quantile \(D_{f,N}\) of Theorem 11.1. This result concerns the ideal family, not content-dependent token rankings, task accuracy or an optimal sparse kernel. At \(\gamma =0\) all sets of that cardinality tie; at negative \(\gamma \) the largest family weights are at the greatest distances. A recent-window interpretation therefore requires the positive-exponent condition.

Continuous approximation and threshold algebra.

For fixed \(0{\lt}\gamma {\lt}1\) and \(0{\lt}f{\lt}1\), the continuous quantile satisfies

\[ D_{f,c}(L)\sim Lf^{1/(1-\gamma )},\qquad \frac{f}{D_{f,c}(L)}\sim \frac{f^{-\gamma /(1-\gamma )}}{L} \quad (L\to \infty ). \]

The second expression is the average retained density, not its boundary threshold. The continuous density at the boundary instead satisfies \(p_c(D_{f,c})\sim (1-\gamma )f^{-\gamma /(1-\gamma )}/L\). An inverse-length dependence in an empirical method such as BLASST blasst2025 does not identify its calibrated coefficient with either expression. The former exponent \(f^{1/(1-\gamma )}\) in the average-density calculation was an algebraic error. Configuration lookup cannot replace the method’s calibration on the basis of this calculation.

Comparison with PyramidKV.

PyramidKV cai2024pyramidkv reports experiments retaining \(12\% \) of the KV cache. Its layer-dependent selection is different from retaining a fixed distance window. To examine the numerical comparison previously made here, take \(\gamma =1.05\) as an illustrative family input, not a Padé prediction: the latter is always below one for positive inputs. At \(N=8192\), the exact continuous formula gives

\[ D_{0.9,c}/N=0.330509,\qquad D_{0.8,c}/N=0.115769,\qquad D_{0.78,c}/N=0.094466. \]

These replace the former \(0.27\), \(0.13\) and asserted \(12\% \) association with \(f=0.78\). Token-distance quantiles use finite sums instead. Neither numerical agreement nor choosing \(f\) after seeing an external budget predicts the external method’s accuracy.

Reasoning and long-context performance.

SnapKV, PyramidKV, H2O and reasoning-focused compression studies snapkv2024,cai2024pyramidkv,zhang2023h2o,holdontothat2025,blasst2025 provide task-specific empirical comparisons. They do not establish that a mass quantile preserves reasoning. The earlier reported benchmark values are preserved in the separate predecessor archive indexed by Appendix J; they were not rerun for this revision. Likewise, \(1/\gamma \) is a threshold-count exponent under the stated family, not a demonstrated geometric dimension that forbids multi-hop reasoning when \(\gamma {\gt}1\). Test quality, retained positions, attention sinks, memory and latency directly for each proposed intervention.

11.5 Shifted-base ratio: scope of the former information-loss expression

Define the algebraic shifted-base coordinate \(b(x)=\theta +x/\sqrt2\). The quantity formerly denoted an information loss is the signed log ratio

\begin{equation} \Delta H_{\rm coord}(D,N) =\log \! \left(\frac{\theta +D/\sqrt2}{\theta +N/\sqrt2}\right), \qquad \theta {\gt}0,\quad 0\le D\le N. \tag {53} \end{equation}
56

It vanishes at \(D=N\) and its algebraic extension to \(D\to 0\) tends to \(\log \theta -\log (\theta +N/\sqrt2)\). This is a difference of logarithms, not the previously printed ratio of logarithms. The expression is nonpositive; it is not established as Shannon entropy loss, KL divergence or task error. The endpoint \(D=0\) is an extension of this coordinate, not a quantile of the continuous support \([1,N]\). Within the coordinate definition the formula is exact and requires no first-order error estimate.

11.6 Soft Horizon Decay: a tested score-bias proposal

The proposed distance weight can be studied as a chosen intervention, without interpreting its cutoff as a physical horizon. For \(h{\gt}0\), \(g{\gt}0\) and causal distance \(d\ge 0\), define

\begin{equation} w(d)=\begin{cases} 1,& d=0,\\ (1-d/h)^g,& 0{\lt}d{\lt}h,\\ 0,& d\ge h. \end{cases} \tag {54} \end{equation}
57

Adding \(\log w(d)\) to pre-softmax scores produces weights proportional to \(w(d)e^{s_{ij}}\), with zero weights represented by a mask. This changes their normalization and mass budget; it is not equivalent to scaling both K and V. Smooth decay of \(w\) does not establish an aliasing mechanism or superior predictions. The available implementation rounds the inverse-coordinate cutoff to an integer and uses a dense four-dimensional mask with eager attention. Its memory consumption is not a measured KV-cache saving.

The archived test used three Pythia models, length 4096, 30 chunks, WikiText-2 test and bf16 in the available script. Pythia’s training context is 2048 tokens, so this is a \(2\times \) extrapolation setting. The elevated full-attention baseline and the improvements under some masks can reflect mitigation of extrapolation failure; they do not establish in-context KV compression. An otherwise matched test at 2048, actual eviction, memory and latency measurements are needed for that claim. The cutoffs for both 1.4B (\(h=2447\)) and 2.8B (\(h=2754\)) exceed 2048; cutoff position alone does not explain their different signs. All four recorded policies are retained below. The column labelled hard \(D_f\) records the window selected by that script, not an empirical quantile of the actual attention matrix.

11.7 Coordinate pruning and the rotary-subspace audit

The original hypothesis proposed that high-index frequency components become redundant beyond \(L_{\rm crit}\). Its prerequisites are unestablished: a failed power-law fit does not identify a semantic layer, and the Shannon entropy bound does not prescribe a sufficient set of positional coordinates. The saved ablations are retained as coordinate interventions with the limitations below.

What the available script changes.

For the fused NeoX projection reshaped as \(W[h,t,r,c]\), with \(t\in \{ Q,K,V\} \), output coordinate \(r\) and input coordinate \(c\), the archived operation is

\begin{equation} W^{(\ell )}[h,Q,r,:]=W^{(\ell )}[h,K,r,:]=0, \quad \ell \ge L_{\rm prune},\quad r\in \{ 2k,2k+1:k_0\le k{\lt}d_{\rm head}/2\} . \tag {55} \end{equation}
61

These are output rows in the stored linear-weight convention, not input columns. The code calculates \(k_0\) from full head dimension and a \(\pi \) threshold, without consulting the partial rotary dimension or pairing.

12 Context Extension: Inverse-Candidate Algebra and Empirical Tests

The configuration-based Padé candidate can be inverted exactly. Its inverse does not establish an optimum for neural-tangent-kernel scaling, retrieval or perplexity. For a specified candidate target \(-1{\lt}g{\lt}1\) and \(T{\gt}0\), define

\begin{equation} \alpha _{\rm cand}=\frac{\theta _{\rm design}(g,T)}{\theta _{\rm nominal}}, \qquad \theta _{\rm design}(g,T)=\frac{T\sqrt2(1+g)}{2(1-g)}. \tag {56} \end{equation}
62

The old notation \(\alpha _{\rm opt}\) is ambiguous: some historical tables use this candidate ratio, whereas the B1 scripts clip a different exponential expression at 64. Neither notation establishes a task optimum. The exponential expression \(e^{C/g}/\theta _{\rm nominal}\) and the linear inverse \(T\sqrt2/(1-g)\) are different functions; neither may replace Equation (56).

For \(T=2048\) and \(\theta _{\rm nominal}=10{,}000\), a target \(g=0.5\) gives \(\theta _{\rm design}=4344.464\) and \(\alpha _{\rm cand}=0.434446\). A target \(g=0.85\) gives \(\theta _{\rm design}=17860.574\) and \(\alpha _{\rm cand}=1.786057\). These correct the rounded arithmetic previously printed as 4346 and 17,858. The nominal candidate is about \(0.7470\); lowering it to \(0.5\) broadens the ideal positive power-law family. It does not establish that the corresponding trained model becomes more global or more local.

Relation to context-extension methods.

In the NTK-aware convention described by peng2023yarn, a context parameter \(s\) changes the base by \(s^{d_r/(d_r-2)}\), for rotary dimension \(d_r{\gt}2\). Thus a base multiplier \(\alpha \) corresponds algebraically to \(s=\alpha ^{(d_r-2)/d_r}\) in that convention; it is not \(s\) itself. YaRN combines a frequency-dependent schedule with attention rescaling and has its own empirical evaluations. A ratio of RoPE bases is not automatically the scaling parameter of those methods. Neither matching a reported scale nor changing a configuration field alone demonstrates the correct runtime rotary transformation. Model-specific implementations and their caches must be checked in any new experiment.

12.1 Designing a candidate base for a specified exponent

Solving the rational equation gives

\begin{equation} \boxed {\theta _{\rm design}(g,T)=\frac{T\sqrt2(1+g)}{2(1-g)}}. \tag {57} \end{equation}
63

Its domain is \(-1{\lt}g{\lt}1\), with the positive-exponent subfamily \(0{\lt}g{\lt}1\) used in the illustrative table. The limit as \(g\to 1^-\) is infinite for this candidate. This is not a theorem that trained models cannot have exponent one at a finite base. Task names previously attached to these targets are removed because the numerical formula does not validate those task assignments.

Testing a candidate setting.

Specify the task and target context before choosing settings. Establish a baseline, implement and verify the actual rotary transformation, and measure both profile changes and task quality under matched data and precision. The previous suggested thresholds \(g\le 0.85\) and \(\alpha \le 8\) are not universal stability constraints. The retained retrieval experiments, including their short-context degradation at a larger tested scale, apply to the conditions reported in Section 18 and Figure 17. The full previous workflow and callback remain in the separate predecessor archive indexed by Appendix J.

Relation to compression.

A candidate target is not a measured exponent. Compute a mass window from a measured profile on the intended support, or explicitly label it a hypothetical family calculation. Task validation remains necessary even if the fitted exponent agrees with the candidate target.

12.2 The former information horizon as an inverse coordinate

The function previously called an information horizon is

\begin{equation} d_{\rm inv}(\theta ,g)=\theta \sqrt2\, \frac{1-g}{1+g}, \qquad \theta {\gt}0,\quad -1{\lt}g{\lt}1. \tag {58} \end{equation}
64

It is the inverse of the candidate with respect to context length. In particular, \(d_{\rm inv}(\theta ,\gamma _P(\theta ,T))=T\) and \(d_{\rm inv}(\theta _{\rm design}(g,T),g)=T\). These equalities are algebraic identities, not independent predictions of training context or retrieval failure. At a fixed \(g\), \(d_{\rm inv}(\alpha \theta ,g)=\alpha d_{\rm inv}(\theta ,g)\), but an intervention need not preserve the fitted exponent. For \(g{\gt}1\) this expression is negative and does not define a physical context length.

The previous example \(\theta =10{,}000\), \(\widehat\gamma =0.748\) gives about 2039 tokens. Its proximity to the 2048-token training context does not establish a universal ceiling. EXP-B1v4 records \(88\% \) at nominal length 3072 and \(10\% \) at 4096 without base scaling; the assertion that it validates \(L^c=2d_{\rm inv}\) is withdrawn. A uniform needle’s expected distance \(L/2\) alone cannot determine a retrieval curve or a collapse threshold. No general impossibility claim for fine-tuning, decoding or prompt changes follows.

For \(z=T\sqrt2/\theta {\gt}0\), the same algebra yields

\[ \log (d_{\rm inv}/T)+\log (z/2)+2\operatorname {arctanh}g=0. \]

The constant depends on the stated definition of \(z\). It is an identity of coordinates, not an empirical invariant of a model.

12.3 Future direction: testing a feedback controller

The original thermostat increased \(\theta \) when a measured exponent exceeded an illustrative target. That direction conflicts with the positive derivative of the candidate in Section 3. A purely candidate-based sign correction would instead use the unvalidated rule

\begin{equation} \theta _{t+1}=\begin{cases} \theta _t/(1+\eta ),& \widehat\gamma _t{\gt}g_*+\delta ,\\ \theta _t,& \text{otherwise}, \end{cases}\qquad \eta {\gt}0. \tag {59} \end{equation}
65

This displayed rule records the direction implied by the candidate only; it is not a recommended implementation. Correcting that sign does not establish the response of a trained network, stability, reduced loss spikes or preserved retrieval. The proposed constants \(g_*=0.85\), \(\delta =0.05\) and \(\eta =0.1\) were illustrative choices without a validated universal operating range.

A useful controlled study would measure the response to small base changes, estimate uncertainty and lag, then compare a prespecified controller with fixed-base and matched-compute baselines. Report instability, loss, task scores and overhead. No such new training experiment or callback implementation is claimed in this revision. The original pseudocode is preserved in the separate predecessor archive indexed by Appendix J.

13 Coordinate Ablations and the Limits of Band Interpretation

The archived interventions remain evidence about particular coordinates and measurement procedures. Their former interpretation as a semantic/positional separation is not supported by the implementation audit. Three distinct operations must be kept separate: the B3 row ablations on Pythia-1B, the amplification script on Pythia-70M, and the coordinate-pruning sweeps in Section 11.7. They do not use the same masks.

13.1 Rotary planes and historical group names

Definition 13.1 Rotary-plane grouping
#
📕 p. 60📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

Let \(d_{\rm rot}=2m\) be the rotary dimension of a head. In the inspected NeoX basis, plane \(k\) contains coordinates \((k,k+m)\), \(0\leq k{\lt}m\); coordinates \(d_{\rm rot},\ldots ,d_{\rm head}-1\) bypass rotation. A complete-cycle classification at \(T\) uses the actual frequencies and the condition \(T\omega _k\geq 2\pi \). It is a geometric count, not a measure of information, usefulness or semantic function. The words zero_dead and zero_alive below identify archived conditions only.

Cite: Definition 13.1, p. 60, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

💡 In plain words

In the inspected NeoX basis, a rotary plane pairs the coordinates \((k,k+m)\); the rest of the head is not rotated. The cycle criterion uses the effective frequencies.

Scope.

The count is geometric. The names of the archived experiments do not prove a semantic partition; the B3 mask did not remove complementary intact planes.

For the frozen Pythia-1B configuration, \(d_{\rm head}=256\), \(d_{\rm rot}=64\), \(m=32\) and there are eight attention heads. The B3 script uses those head dimensions, but zeros adjacent pairs instead of the split-half planes. For each head, it correctly locates the fused Q and K weight blocks and selects coordinates \(0{:}46\) for zero_dead, or \(46{:}64\) for zero_alive, using half-open intervals. The first mask removes both weight rows of 14 rotary planes and one row of each of the other 18; the second removes one row of those same 18 planes. Thus the masks are unequal coordinate interventions, not complementary sets of intact frequency planes. Projection biases and V weights are not changed; zeroed weight rows do not by themselves guarantee zero post-projection activations. These statements were checked by executing the archived mask and restore functions on synthetic weights. They do not reconstruct the historical runtime.

Within a fixed window it reuses the same random seed and target-sampling rule across conditions. Across windows the sampling interval changes, so the sampled targets are not paired. The prefix grows from \(W\) to \(W+31\) during the target block; \(W\) is the starting context length. The JSON stores aggregate PPL, not per-target losses or confidence intervals.

There is a separate intervention error. The script treats fused NeoX rows as three contiguous model-wide Q, K and V blocks, but the actual layout is head, Q/K/V, coordinate. On a synthetic tensor with the configured dimensions, the function scales 276 Q rows, 230 K rows and 230 V rows per layer. Q heads 0–5 are affected, K/V heads 0–4 are affected, and heads 6–7 are untouched. In each affected component it selects the first 46 coordinates; Pythia-70M has only 16 rotary coordinates per head. This is neither a Q/K-only operation nor a rotary-only operation.

The observed changes relative to \(\alpha =1\) are approximately \(-0.041926\), \(-0.101578\) and \(-0.067026\). Their sign is opposite to the simulation’s increases \(0.15\), \(0.36\) and \(0.70\). The baseline being largest among four settings does not establish an optimum: no task-quality objective, local two-sided search or uncertainty is supplied, and the saved WikiText PPL entries are NaN. The claim that trained weights occupy a geometric optimum is withdrawn. Matching a configuration formula cannot repair the mask.

Output projection sparsity.

The former \(W_O\) experiment reported less than \(1.3\% \) throughput change after dense zeroing and a roughly sevenfold PPL increase on random tokens. These remain historical reports, not a validated frequency-pruning result. RoPE rotates Q/K, not V; the input coordinates of \(W_O\) therefore have no direct “dead RoPE band” assignment. Zero entries in an unchanged dense matrix do not imply a measured FLOP, latency or memory reduction. The suggested \(3.5\times \) projection saving and the mechanism attributed to Q-ROAR are not established by this record. A sparse backend, matched task evaluation and an explicit coordinate map would be separate experiments.

What a discriminating follow-up requires.

Read the rotary dimension and actual pairing, verify fused QKV layout, hold V and nonrotary coordinates fixed, and compare equal-size masks of complete planes with randomized controls. Record whether biases are intervened on. Use the same target positions across context windows and store per-example losses; measure positional and content tasks separately. Until those tests exist, the saved effects support coordinate sensitivity, not a semantic reservoir, double dissociation or safe band-pruning rule.

14 Attention Profiles, Weight Ratios and Circuit Hypotheses

14.1 A conditional reference distribution is not a circuit detector

For each query \(i\), choose a nonempty set \(J_i\) of past keys, excluding self if \(d^{-g}\) is used. Normalize observed and reference weights on the same set:

\[ p_{ij}=\frac{a_{ij}}{\sum _{k\in J_i}a_{ik}},\qquad q_{ij}=\frac{(i-j)^{-g}}{\sum _{k\in J_i}(i-k)^{-g}}. \]

Positive retained observed mass is required. Report the excluded sink/self mass, query selection and fitting protocol. The per-head statistic is

\begin{equation} \kappa _{h,\ell }=\operatorname {KL}(p^{h,\ell }\Vert q), \tag {60} \end{equation}
68

with any averaging across queries stated explicitly. MaxEnt characterizes \(q\) under its specified constraint; it does not prove that \(q\) is attention with semantic content removed. A nonzero KL can result from sinks, local structure, masking or reference misspecification. A small KL does not identify the function of the value vectors. Neither statistic identifies an induction circuit without separate task and intervention evidence.

The former screening recipe used 50 prompts, a \(0.05\) threshold, and claimed fewer than \(15\% \) of heads were flagged across nine models. These are historical screening settings and reports, not validated sensitivity, specificity or a sixfold reduction in the cost of discovering circuits. The earlier \(0.1\) “SWA sink” threshold also has no calibrated causal interpretation. A window cannot truncate a sequence shorter than itself; the 4096-window Mistral configuration cannot explain a window-boundary effect in the short sequences examined here. A held-out labelled benchmark and matched masked/unmasked controls would be needed for a detection claim.

14.2 Weight-space measurements: coordinates and averaging

The saved spectral scripts group adjacent output coordinates over the full head dimension. The TransformerLens version uses columns of tensors stored as (head, input, output); the raw-Hugging-Face version uses rows of the linear-weight matrix. For a coordinate group \(I_k\), their Frobenius-product statistic is

\[ E_{\ell h k}=\| W_{Q,\ell h}[I_k,:]\| _F \| W_{K,\ell h}[I_k,:]\| _F. \]

This is a product of norms, not a variance-based signal-to-noise ratio. The inspected Pythia configs have partial RoPE and the inspected NeoX implementation uses split-half pairing. The archived full-head adjacent groups cannot be relabelled as true rotary planes by inverting their ratio. For TransformerLens exports, the conversion/permutation must additionally be verified; its historical version is not frozen in the experiment record.

Let \(a_{\ell h}\) and \(b_{\ell h}\) be the means of \(E_{\ell h k}\) below and above the archived cutoff. The saved summary is

\[ M_{\rm hist}=\frac{1}{LH}\sum _{\ell ,h}\frac{a_{\ell h}}{b_{\ell h}}, \qquad R_{\rm hist}=1/M_{\rm hist}. \]

In general neither equals the opposite-direction mean ratio or a ratio of grand means. For Pythia-1B, \(M_{\rm hist}=0.900342\), \(R_{\rm hist}=1.110689\), while the mean of \(b/a\) is \(1.113334\) and the ratio of group grand means \(a/b\) is \(0.894128\). For Pythia-70M, the corresponding \(M_{\rm hist}\) and grand-mean ratio are \(0.872883\) and \(0.800258\). The aggregation convention matters.

The two GQA aggregate records.

The separate Qwen file reports global ratios \(0.903216\) (0.5B) and \(0.880607\) (3B), while its layer-ratio means are \(0.883547\) and \(0.877954\). Correlations and the meaning of \(M\).

Across the five saved Pythia records, Pearson correlations with \(d_{\rm head}\) are \(r(M_{\rm hist},d_{\rm head})=+0.987556\) and \(r(R_{\rm hist},d_{\rm head})=-0.986580\). The latter is a strong negative sample correlation, not a weak or partial correlation. These five sizes do not control for architecture, training or the changed coordinate grouping. The historical multivariate expression \(1.13+0.0009d_{\rm head}-0.008\log _{10}\theta \) predicts \(1.3284\) for Pythia-1B, not its stored \(1.110689\); it is not retained as a fitted predictor. The five Pythia values of \(M_{\rm hist}\) range from \(0.872883\) to \(0.900342\), and the eight-model panel ranges from \(0.787101\) to \(0.900342\). Combining the two Qwen global ratios gives a heterogeneous ten-model range up to \(0.903216\), not \([0.72,0.90]\).

\(M\) denotes an explicitly defined coordinate norm ratio only. \(M=1\) is parity under that definition, not a reasoning/memory boundary, semantic capacity or fractal packing transition. The normalized architecture score \(\widehat M\) has no validated predictive baseline and is withdrawn as a comparison rule. Figure 15 retains the seven historical points, with corrected values and descriptive axes; its exponents and ratios come from different protocols and do not constitute an architecture taxonomy.

Software consistency.

The local tools/taf/diagnose/m_score.py is not an implementation of the archived statistic. It averages Q/K norms rather than multiplying them, uses a different complementary cutoff formula, and splits the fused NeoX tensor into three model-wide blocks. A synthetic row-identity check recovers only 256 of 2048 expected Q rows and none of the expected K rows for the 1B shape. It also omits the partial-rotary restriction. Its output must not be cited as a reproduction of these tables. This manuscript audit does not modify or certify the deployed software; source snapshots and the synthetic checks are included in the reproducibility package.

Extended historical exponent panel.

The 26-point map retains its historical panel, with the Pythia-2.8B contrast corrected to the matched 30–100 grid. Its cross-protocol and architecture claims require reconciliation with the row-level evidence; no induction threshold, SWA mechanism or controller prescription is inferred.

14.3 The \(\gamma \)-Field: Heterogeneity and Its Instrument Null

The available field extractor measures the last query at sequence length \(d+60\), always against key 59. It averages randomly generated token prompts at each distance, then fits each layer/head separately. This is neither the fixed-query October QL protocol nor the \(d+50\) E4 procedure. Its causal uniform profile is

\[ A_0(d)=\frac{1}{d+60}. \]

Executing the actual extractor and fitter on synthetic causal-uniform matrices gives \(\widehat\gamma _0=0.755252\), \(R^2=0.985521\) on \(\{ 30,50,100,200,500,1000,2000\} \). With the six-point grid ending at 1000 the null slope is \(0.710309\). The five saved records use different prompt counts and, for 2.8B, a different grid; those settings are part of the observation, not interchangeable replications.

All five use seeds 42 and 123. Counts in the table are prompts per seed and distance. The JSON stores fitted matrices, not per-distance attention arrays or prompt-level outcomes. The means and standard deviations above are recalculated over finite fitted cells. The script accepts a head if at least three distance means are finite and exceed \(10^{-12}\); it applies no \(R^2\) acceptance threshold. A NaN marks failure of that numerical/data criterion, not an identified semantic head or failure of a power-law goodness-of-fit test.

Pythia-70M has 18 NaN cells: two in L3 and eight each in L4 and L5, using zero-based indices. L4–L5 alone account for \(16/48=33.3\% \), not the full \(37.5\% \). Pythia-410M also has \(37.5\% \) NaNs, all 16 heads of each layer L15–L23. This panel does not identify an induction threshold at 400 million parameters or establish \(L_{\rm crit}\) from missing fits.

The global fit is below the finite-cell mean in all five records. The distance-dependent mixture derivative in Section 10 explains why averaging slopes differs from fitting a mixture, but does not prove that these measured profiles are exact power-law components or that the reported global slope is an asymptotic tail exponent. The global nanmean also permits the participating head set to vary by distance. Head-specific null corrections would require each accepted support and weighting; the common null must not be subtracted indiscriminately from cells fitted on fewer points.

The outlier rule in the script is mean \(\pm 2\) standard deviations, not fixed thresholds of \(0.1\) and \(2\). For the 1B record, the saved high heads are (L0,H4) \(2.204\), (L1,H3) \(2.772\) and (L3,H0) \(1.810\), and the low head is (L1,H0) \(0.077\). The 2.8B record contains a maximum of \(7.389\) in L30,H0; L30 is penultimate, not the last attention layer. Flagging a head does not exclude it from the reported global fit or identify its task. The inverse association between head dimension and field dispersion is descriptive; it does not follow from a Riemann-sum argument or isolate training-induced specialization.

The different averaging populations explain why mean \(R^2\) can be below the selection threshold. Class labels use decoded-token heuristics and token-ID cutoffs (COMMON below 1000, RARE above 30000), not measured corpus frequency bins. The number stored as total queries sums contributions across distances and heads; it is not a count of distinct independent queries. Selected head sets differ between classes, so their medians are not paired contrasts and do not establish multifractality.

Although context length is fixed, the eligible query pool changes with distance: a query \(q\) contributes only if \(q\ge d\). For uniform causal attention the class-specific mean is the average of \(1/(q+1)\) over that distance’s eligible class queries, and need not be flat. The saved fit matrices omit query positions and per-distance class counts, preventing an exact matched lexical-null reconstruction. These limitations also apply to interpreting the exploratory cross-family summaries. The median spread \(.921402-.612941=.308461\) is descriptive, not a measured geometric dimension or a critical fluctuation.

15 Base/Instruct Comparisons Under a Variable-Length Probe

15.1 Estimand, protocol and provenance

We use \(\delta \gamma =\widehat\gamma _{\rm instruct}-\widehat\gamma _{\rm base}\) for a checkpoint contrast. This is distinct from the random-minus-text corpus contrast \(\Delta \gamma \) in Section 16, and from a residual against \(\gamma _P\). The eight D3 pairs are retained as reported observations; they do not isolate reinforcement learning from SFT, DPO or other changes. An instruction checkpoint is not by itself evidence that RLHF was used.

The available cloud_d3_rlhf_kaggle.py specifies 50 random-token prompts per distance, seed 42, fp16 and eager attention. It generates lengths \(n=d+60\), reads the final query at key position 59 (zero-based), pools finite head/layer attention values, and fits OLS in log space at \(d\in \{ 30,50,100,200,500,1000\} \). Distances 10 and 20 are measured but not fitted. Uniform causal attention therefore yields

\[ A_0(d)=\frac1{d+60},\qquad \widehat\gamma _0=0.7103091963,\qquad R_0^2=0.984052729. \]

This is the matched D3 null, not the \(d+50\) E4 null. The actual fitting function and an independent 50-digit calculation agree. No new checkpoint inference was run. Subtracting this common null from both slopes leaves their difference unchanged; it does not remove model-dependent sinks, token effects or missing attention values.

The manuscript’s eight-pair table is the available D3 numerical summary. Its full d3_rlhf_results.json was not located in the searched local results and experiment directories. The instruct column and three base entries therefore retain rounded-manuscript provenance. Five base values have a recoverable numerical counterpart in the round-2 random-token arrays: SmolLM2-1.7B (\(0.866259\)), Qwen2.5-0.5B (\(0.906234\)), Qwen2.5-1.5B (\(0.980402\)), Qwen2.5-3B (\(0.746480\)), and Llama-3.2-3B (\(0.678947\)). All reproduce the D3 base entries after rounding to three decimals. The two available scripts share the random-token rule, \(d+60\), seed 42, 50 prompts, fit grid and fp16 setting for these models. This establishes reproducible counterpart values under matching declared protocols, but matching rounded values does not prove that D3 reused those exact runs. It does not reconstruct the missing instruct arrays or paired uncertainty. A separate April 21 two-pair JSON reports different values and remains a separate experiment. The script’s planned panel also contains a Phi-3 self-pair (the same checkpoint twice); that entry is not an independent base/instruct pair and is not included in the eight rows.

15.2 What the reported differences support

At the explicitly chosen descriptive cutoff \(0.02\), the correct counts are two increases, three decreases and three small changes. “Small” means \(|\delta \gamma |\leq 0.02\) in this table, not statistically indistinguishable or mechanistically unchanged. The largest reported absolute change is \(0.072\); no displayed pair crosses one. These are properties of eight rounded estimates, not bounds on post-training or evidence for a phase barrier. Opposite signs in the two Llama-3.2 pairs do not identify which recipe component caused either shift. A negligible scalar shift does not show that learning acted only on MLPs or output logits.

The script resets the random generator for each checkpoint. Identical token sequences within a pair additionally require equal tokenizer vocabulary bounds; the archived summary does not establish all tokenizer revisions. Across distances, the generator advances and the inputs differ. Per-prompt attention profiles and loss/task outcomes were not recovered for D3, so this audit cannot construct paired confidence intervals or assess whether the chosen cutoff exceeds sampling variability. No preregistration record or independent test set supports the former correlation and early-warning claims.

Consequences for monitoring.

The exponent can be recorded alongside loss and task metrics under an invariant instrument, but predictive monitoring requires prospective validation. The previous \(C_V{\gt}20\) catastrophic-forgetting alarm is withdrawn: at \(N=2000\) the finite-family maximum is approximately \(6.92\). Neither the eight pairs nor their size ordering establishes a \(4\times 10^8\) induction-head threshold, alignment quality, safety, or a universal post-training effect.

16 Corpus Contrasts and the Unvalidated Architecture Ratio

16.1 A descriptive statistic with a fixed sign convention

Definition 16.1 Matched corpus contrast
#
📕 p. 70📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

For a specified checkpoint, precision, attention implementation, distance grid and length/query rule, define

\begin{equation} \Delta \gamma =\widehat\gamma _{\rm random}-\widehat\gamma _{\rm text}. \end{equation}
69

Cite: Definition 16.1, p. 70, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

💡 In plain words

The contrast subtracts the exponent fitted on text from the one fitted on random tokens. Its sign is interpreted only if checkpoint, precision, implementation, distance grid and query rule have been matched.

Scope.

The sign alone does not identify a circuit, an architecture or a cause of the observed difference.

A positive contrast means a steeper fitted random-token profile and a flatter text profile on that support; a negative contrast means the converse. Neither sign identifies an architecture or an induction circuit. A residual against \(\gamma _P\) is a different quantity and must not be substituted here. Matching the instrument is necessary; it does not make corpora, tokenizers or training histories exchangeable across models.

The earlier comparison actually lists five model entries, not seven; Falcon has no pair of exponents in that table. These summaries are retained as a separate panel from the cloud rounds below. Pythia-70M’s duplicated \(0.748\) does not establish equality across corpora; the matched-grid analysis in Section 8.4 takes precedence for that comparison. Likewise Llama-3-8B values \(-0.287\), \(-0.115\) and \(-0.034\) appearing in different records are not repeat estimates under an established common protocol. Qwen2.5-3B’s \(+0.192\), \(-0.225\) and \(-0.053\) must not be merged into a single architecture signature. The record and its grid must accompany each value.

Google’s reference Gemma-2-9B configuration has 16 query heads, 8 KV heads, \(d_{\rm head}=256\), and an alternating local/global pattern with local window 4096; thus \(G=n_q/n_{\rm kv}=2\), not 8. 1 Falcon-7B uses RoPE and multi-query attention, rather than ALiBi, as recorded in the configuration audit. Mistral-7B-v0.1’s configured window is also 4096. For sequences of at most 2050 tokens in the earlier E4 panel, or 1060 tokens in the cloud protocol, a 4096-token local mask excludes no additional causal keys. Therefore an active sliding-window cutoff cannot explain these measured differences. Training with local attention could still affect the learned weights; that separate hypothesis was not tested by these comparisons.

The old sign-based decision tree and the claim that configuration files can be replaced by two scalar fits are withdrawn. Architecture should be read from the exact configuration and implementation. Circuit identification needs behavioral and intervention evidence, such as the small-model experiments of olsson2022induction; their work does not supply a universal \(4\times 10^8\)-parameter threshold.

16.3 Cloud rounds: shared estimator, different evidence depth

The round-2 and round-3 scripts use 50 prompts, seed 42, the \(d+60\) rule and the same six fitted distances as D3. They compare random IDs with contiguous WikiText-2 training-text chunks, averaged across finite head/layer values. Text chunks are sampled anew by length; random and text prompts are not paired semantic counterparts. Precision varies by model, and round 4 uses 4-bit NF4 for Mistral. The matched uniform null is again \(0.7103091963\).

There is an additional provenance hazard: the round-2/3 text-loading failure path reuses the random result as “text”. That branch forces \(\Delta \gamma =0\) without measuring text. We do not claim it occurred in the successful rows below, whose corpus estimates differ; future outputs must record corpus-load success explicitly and treat fallback as missing, rather than neutral.

The archive provides full distance means for six successful round-2 models and Mistral in round 4. All fourteen corpus fits and their \(R^2\) values replay to numerical precision. Round 3 provides rounded summaries for Pythia-2.8B, Llama-3-8B and a repeat of Llama-3.2-3B. The last is not counted as a new model. For Llama-3-8B the displayed \(0.821-0.856=-0.035\), while the saved rounded contrast is \(-0.034\); we preserve the latter as reported, without inventing unavailable digits. Failed loads and incomplete models are not measurements.

16.4 Recomputing the proposed ratio

The historical heuristic was

\begin{equation} R_c=\frac{\log (d_{\rm head}/n_{\rm kv})}{\log (N/N_0)}, \qquad N_0=4\times 10^8.\tag {62} \end{equation}
70

Here \(N_0\) is a chosen reference scale, not an established induction threshold. The numerator is not the GQA sharing factor \(n_q/n_{\rm kv}\) and is not a measured channel capacity. The mathematical ratio is singular at \(N=N_0\); the archived helper additionally returns NaN for \(N\leq N_0\) or \(n_{\rm kv}\geq d_{\rm head}\). Those software restrictions are not physical boundaries. The previous MHA example incorrectly dropped \(n_{\rm kv}\): with \(d_{\rm head}=64\), eight KV heads and \(N=10^9\), the ratio is \(\log 8/\log 2.5\simeq 2.269\), not \(\log 64/\log 2.5\simeq 4.539\).

The failed Gemma row’s archived \(n_{\rm kv}=16\) is incorrect (the reference configuration has eight), and is not promoted into a successful observation. 16.5 What fails, and what remains untested

Using the sign of the nine reported contrasts, the minimum–maximum ranges are

\[ R_c(\Delta \gamma {\gt}0)\in [0.472621,17.077567],\qquad R_c(\Delta \gamma {\lt}0)\in [0.924358,3.085057]. \]

Their interval intersection is \([0.924358,3.085057]\). This is an intersection of two sample range hulls, not a densely measured zone, confidence interval, phase boundary or evidence that every point in it supports both signs. The previous intervals \([0.4,1.0]\), \([0.47,1.33]\) and \([0.5,1.3]\) do not represent that calculation. Classification cutoffs also changed historically between zero, \(0.02\) and \(0.1\); they must not be mixed. Here signs are descriptive and no “pre-IH” or “post-IH” ground-truth labels are assigned.

The statement “all models with \(R_c\geq 2\) have negative contrast” is false: Qwen2.5-0.5B has \(R_c=17.077567\) and \(\Delta \gamma =+0.044788\). Its proximity to the chosen singular reference scale explains sensitivity of the ratio, not permission to remove the counterexample after seeing it. Llama-3-8B and Mistral have negative contrasts below one, while Pythia-2.8B and SmolLM2-1.7B have positive contrasts there. These selected heterogeneous models do not establish a monotone rule or a causal effect of KV sharing.

At fixed \(d_{\rm head}\) and \(n_{\rm kv}\) with positive numerator and \(N{\gt}N_0\),

\[ \frac{\partial R_c}{\partial N} =-\frac{\log (d_{\rm head}/n_{\rm kv})}{N[\log (N/N_0)]^2}{\lt}0. \]

Thus the earlier advice to raise \(N\) to raise \(R_c\) was algebraically reversed. Lowering \(n_{\rm kv}\) does raise this ratio, but the archive does not show that doing so improves induction, quality, safety or training efficiency. The ratio-based architecture prescriptions and their \(\alpha _S\) extension are withdrawn; Appendix H preserves their definitions and examples as an unvalidated historical construction.

An adequate follow-up would pin checkpoint/config/tokenizer/library revisions, hold precision and contexts fixed, record per-sequence profiles and corpus-load status, and compare candidate decay families on held-out sequences. Confidence intervals should resample sequences, not treat heads or distances as independent replicates. A causal KV-head claim additionally requires a controlled architectural intervention and direct circuit/task outcomes. Neither a sign contrast nor a good in-sample log–log fit supplies those tests.

17 Diagnostic Manual and Model Encyclopaedia

Revision of 7 November 2026

The model encyclopaedia and command examples remain for continuity. Their configuration, measurement and recommendation fields must be distinguished. Do not fill a missing measured exponent with a configuration formula or treat a historical “safe”/“requires NTK” verdict as a current recommendation. The software interface and model metadata may have changed; this revision does not assert that all printed commands or current remote outputs were retested.

17.1 Using the archived diagnostic CLI

The November 5 snapshot contains cli/diagnose_model.py. Its example command, relative to that software checkout, is 

python cli/diagnose_model.py --model EleutherAI/pythia-70m --fast --cpu

The inspected snapshot defines four fast distances \(10,50,200,1000\) and 30 attempted prompts per distance, not 20. Full mode attempts 80 prompts per distance on the nine-point grid

\[ 10,20,30,50,100,200,500,1000,2000. \]

Successful fits depend on available attention outputs and valid samples. Its recorded protocol uses lengths \(d+50\) and the final query, so the matched-null cautions apply. Runtime, CPU memory and model support depend on the actual checkpoint, libraries and hardware; the old three-/fifteen-minute universal promises are withdrawn. Quantization is an optional backend with its own requirements, not a guarantee for every model above a size threshold. Printed commands are source documentation, not commands executed in this audit.

17.2 Measurement Decision Guide

Record the exact checkpoint/configuration, tokenizer, precision, attention implementation, corpus, length/query rule, seeds, distance support and aggregation. Compute a matched null through the same estimator. Fit alternative decay families and inspect residuals on held-out sequences; a low power-law \(R^2\) does not identify ALiBi or SWA. Report corpus contrasts without mapping their signs to architectures.

Observation

Follow-up

Poor power-law fit

Inspect support, masks, sinks and competing families; do not infer architecture from \(R^2\).

Fit near or above one

Compute finite-support quantities; validate any cache policy with task outcomes.

Nonzero corpus contrast

Preserve both estimates and their uncertainty; check matched metadata and corpus-load success.

Head or layer heterogeneity

Inspect individual profiles; establish circuit function with direct tests.

Large mass quantile

Treat as a distributional calculation, not a guarantee of useful retained context.

The previous threshold flowchart is superseded by this measurement-first guide; its exact text and diagram source remain in the revision archive.

17.3 Architecture Design: Withdrawn Scalar Prescriptions

The earlier five-step tree mapped task names to target exponents, inverted \(\gamma _P\) for a RoPE base, required \(R_c\geq 2\), and used \(\alpha _S\) to decide whether to train. These prescriptions are withdrawn. The cloud panel contains a positive-contrast model above \(R_c=17\); the claimed induction threshold is not established; and raising model size lowers the written ratio under its usual positive-domain assumptions (Section 16.4). An algebraic inverse of a candidate fit is not a validated architecture controller.

Choose context, memory, latency and quality requirements explicitly, then compare actual implementations on representative held-out tasks. A pilot should measure uncertainty and compare a baseline before selecting KV sharing, RoPE scaling or a cache policy. These measurements cannot be replaced by a scalar “ignition” score.

The associated hardware proposal also lacks support from the archived band ablations: their masks do not select complementary rotary-plane classes and one implementation changes V (Sections 14.2 and 13.4). The historical estimates of 25% attention compute and 7–15% total energy savings are proposals, not measured kernel speedups or quality-preserving guarantees. Correct plane indexing, an implemented sparse kernel and end-to-end quality/throughput measurements would be needed.

Each row stipulates a power family on \(1,\ldots ,2000\); this extrapolation is not a new attention measurement. To make the lookup exactly reproducible, the inputs are the six-decimal displayed exponents of Table 10. The discrete column is the smallest integer capturing at least \(.9\) of that family’s mass; the continuous column uses Lebesgue measure on \([1,2000]\). Neither is a quality-preserving cache prescription.

18 Limitations and Open Questions

Revision of 7 November 2026

The original limitations, tables and failure atlas are retained, with additional limits stated locally. The Phase-A-only restriction on the finite continuous quantile is corrected: it is finite for all real \(\gamma \), with \(N^f\) at one. The main withdrawn claims are the geometric derivation of the learned exponent, independent inverse-horizon validation and task guarantees from mass alone. The 17 missing October observations and incomplete weight provenance are unresolved. The additions reuse saved evidence and do not repair it by inference.

We list the principal limitations of the framework honestly and in one place.

L1: the proposed geometric derivation is not established.

The power-law family follows conditionally from a log-distance score or a prescribed MaxEnt constraint; rotary cycle counts alone imply neither. The Padé candidate has no accepted universal derivation. Selected-panel error percentages do not repair its invalid boundary conditions or nonlinear averaging step (Appendix B).

L2: position scheme is not an empirical family diagnosis.

GPT-2 has absolute positions; BLOOM has ALiBi; Falcon-7B has RoPE/MQA. The finite power-family quantile is mathematical for any exponent, conditional on that family. No positional encoding by itself validates the family or a task-level cache or context-extension guarantee.

L3: coordinate effects do not establish frequency-specific functions.

The revised Sections 13 and 14.2 separate the B3 masks, GPU amplification, coordinate pruning and norm-ratio statistics. The historical B3 labels are not complete-plane interventions; its two masks affect different numbers of coordinates. The amplification script also changes V and leaves heads untouched. The full-head spectral summaries do not isolate the partial rotary subspace. Their effects and correlations therefore cannot validate a semantic reservoir, a geometric optimum or safe pruning. The original \(1.38\) and \(0.87\) labels must not be merged with the audited 1B \(M_{\rm hist}=0.900342\) and its reciprocal \(1.110689\). No new model run is claimed by the synthetic tensor checks or aggregate replays.

L4: base/instruct evidence is limited.

The eight-pair D3 manuscript summary has two increases, three decreases and three small changes at cutoff \(0.02\) (Section 15). Its raw output was not located; the available script gives the matched uniform null \(0.710309\). An earlier two-pair JSON is separate evidence. These observations do not isolate RLHF or validate attention-based warnings of forgetting or alignment changes.

L5: mathematical scope versus empirical use.

The finite continuous mass quantile applies to every real exponent, with \(N^f\) at one. The \(g{\lt}1\) large-\(N\) approximation can be inaccurate near one. A mass quantile does not guarantee task quality, and the variable-length E4 instrument produces a nonzero slope even for uniform attention.

L6: saved KV, base-scaling and retrieval experiments.

The complete two-model and seven-model B2 panels remain separate in Section 11. They test asymptotic windows with different target blocks and do not validate a universal favorable exponent interval. The B1 experiments below change a nominal RoPE base before loading the same weights; they do not fine-tune those weights. Their \(\alpha \) denotes the base multiplier, not the context-extension factor of every method called NTK scaling.

EXP-B1v3: long-sequence PPL and its denominator.

The saved Pythia-1B record has four base settings and four 64-token target bands, indexed from zero as \([960,1024)\), \([1984,2048)\), \([3008,3072)\) and \([4032,4096)\). The script requests up to ten 4096-token WikiText-2 test segments and supplies the whole prefix up to each band’s end. Thus 4096 is sequence length, not the number of sequences. The JSON preserves aggregate PPL, not per-sequence losses or immutable execution metadata. Pythia-1B was trained at 2048: bands A and B end within that context, whereas C and D test extrapolation. Their very large unscaled losses are not an in-context compression baseline.
