The historical ratios divide each setting’s B/C/D PPL by its own A PPL. They compare different target bands and suppress changes in the denominator. At \(\alpha =4\), A rises from 11.949197 to 13.877564 (\(+16.14\% \)), and B from 12.659133 to 14.549244 (\(+14.93\% \)), compared with \(\alpha =1\) on the same band. Its C and D PPL are much lower than the unscaled values. This is a recorded short/long-context tradeoff, not cost-free extension. The historical \(1.80\times \) at \(\alpha =64\) is B/A within that setting; B is instead \(11.34\times \) the unscaled B value. No paired uncertainty can be recovered from these aggregates.

The value 64 comes from clipping the legacy expression \(e^{\log (10000)/0.5}/10000=10000\) at 64. It is neither the inverse-candidate value \(0.434446\) at \(T=2048\) nor a demonstrated optimum. The data contain no fine-tuning test that could validate this prescription after weight adaptation. YaRN uses a different schedule and attention rescaling peng2023yarn; its results do not certify this base multiplier.

Earlier B1 protocols remain distinct.

The v2 PPL script crops 124, 148 or 150 context tokens plus 64 target tokens and supplies no offset position IDs: its inputs are only 188–214 tokens long. The large source-text offsets therefore do not test long positional contexts. All 20 v2 PPL aggregates are preserved in the evidence package. The original NIAH record contains 25 cells of \(0/40\) at five lengths and five base settings. Its next-token argmax criterion, comparing only the first token of each separately tokenized key, differs from the subsequent candidate-ranking task; the zero counts are retained, not discarded as failed measurements or pooled with v4/v5.

EXP-B1v4/v5: deterministic candidate-ranking NIAH.

The scripts score a correct numeric key against nine distractor entries in repeated laboratory-themed filler. The 50 insertion fractions form a fixed grid from 0.1 to 0.9; they are not random needle positions. Keys and distractors are selected deterministically from a tokenizer-filtered pool. A tie with a distractor counts as failure. This is restricted candidate ranking, not free-generation retrieval or reasoning. The model records retain historical exponent tags \(.748\), \(.931\), \(.705\) and \(.674\) for Pythia-70M, 1B, 1.4B and 2.8B, respectively. The v5 retrieval script does not remeasure these exponents after changing the base.

A reconstruction using the frozen local Pythia-70M tokenizer produces 75 pool entries but only 61 distinct keys; the first 50 trials use 42 distinct keys, and some trials have eight distinct distractors among the nine entries. The pool builder does not deduplicate and only uses its three-digit fallback if fewer than 20 entries were found. All reconstructed context lengths are \(L+1\) because BOS is added after the filler budget; scoring adds the key token as well. These are properties of the saved code with the specified tokenizer snapshot, not proof of the exact historical runtime. The aggregate JSON omits the token IDs, runtime frequency buffers, per-trial scores and immutable library/weight revisions needed for that stronger claim.

The plotted \(10\% \) line is the nominal reference for ten exchangeable candidate entries. Deterministic, duplicated and differently frequent keys do not establish that reference as the model’s measured no-needle accuracy. No matched no-needle or shuffled-label control is saved here. Reused keys and filler also prevent treating the 50 trials as independent corpus samples. We report counts without manufacturing paired significance from aggregates.

At nominal \(L=4096\), unscaled accuracies are \(10,16,12,24\% \); at \(\alpha =4\) they are \(86,100,100,100\% \). At \(\alpha =8\) they are \(88,100,100,100\% \). The three larger models reach \(50/50\) under both 4 and 8; this observed ceiling is not a guarantee of population accuracy.

There is no strict Pareto dominance by \(\alpha =4\): on Pythia-70M it loses two percentage points against \(\alpha =1\) at both 1024 and 2048, and at 4096 it trails \(\alpha =8\) by two points. The \(\alpha =16\) Pythia-2.8B row remains at \(100\% \) at every tested length, contradicting a universal over-extension failure at 16. The large unscaled drops do not by themselves identify rotary aliasing as their cause. They support the recorded restricted-task comparison, not an exponent-derived optimum, a universal safe interval, or the threshold \(L^c=2d_{\rm inv}\).

figureSaved candidate-ranking accuracies for Pythia-70M (EXP-B1v4; 50 deterministic trials per cell). The v5 small-model panel is identical. Coordinates retain every reported value; \(\alpha \) is a base multiplier. The nominal ten-candidate reference is not a measured no-needle baseline. At \(L=4096\), \(\alpha =4\) scores \(43/50\) and \(\alpha =8\) scores \(44/50\). At 1024 and 2048, \(\alpha =4\) scores \(45/50\) versus \(46/50\) unscaled. These observations do not prove a universal optimum or an aliasing mechanism.

L7: the finite-family heat capacity is not sampling-temperature response.

nakaishi2024critical study correlations and critical behavior in generated text as the token-sampling temperature varies. That work does not establish the negative heat-capacity claim formerly attributed to it here; the attribution is withdrawn. Its sampling variable and observables differ from the fixed-support distance family used in this manuscript.

Our finite-family quantity is

\[ C_V(\gamma ,N)=\gamma ^2\partial _\gamma ^2\log Z_N(\gamma ) =\gamma ^2\operatorname {Var}_{p_\gamma }(\log d),\qquad Z_N(\gamma )=\sum _{d=1}^N d^{-\gamma }. \]

It is nonnegative and finite for every real exponent at fixed finite \(N\). Only for fixed \(\gamma {\gt}1\) does the infinite-support normalizer tend to \(\zeta (\gamma )\); in that limiting family \(C_V\) diverges as \(\gamma \to 1^+\). For \(N=2000\), the positive-exponent finite maximum is instead near \(\gamma =1.256885\), with \(C_V=6.919812\). The factor \(\gamma ^2\) is essential: variance alone is Fisher information, not heat capacity. None of these identities supplies the response of token sampling or a physical transition in a trained model.

L8: mixture-of-experts needs architecture-specific definitions.

An expert need not own a separate attention operator. For example, Mixtral’s experts are feedforward blocksmixtral2024audit. A per-expert attention exponent therefore cannot be assumed from the term MoE. Routing-conditioned profile comparisons would need explicit query populations and controlled measurements; the inverse candidate does not validate a per-expert horizon.

L9: a single fitted exponent loses heterogeneity.

The field measurements in Section 14.3 retain head/layer variation and missing fits. A global family is a modeling choice. High family heat capacity need not occur exactly at one, and neither a fitted exponent nor a proxy gate establishes a head’s task sensitivity. Direct interventions and paired outcomes remain necessary.

L10: the original falsification claims do not survive this audit.

The proposed universal geometric predictor already fails the initial mixed-panel comparison and does not reproduce the October QL comparison. Those observations do not satisfy the earlier claimed five-percent error criterion. The E4 null also shows that a fitted power law does not require rotary geometry. Comparing different model families cannot isolate the effect of replacing a positional encoding; such a causal test needs matched training and measurement controls.

A negative relation between \(g\) and entropy computed from the same positive-\(g\) finite family is algebraic: \(\mathrm{d}H/\mathrm{d}g=-g\operatorname {Var}(\log d)\). It is not an independent empirical test of a physical entropy mechanism. The appropriate empirical objects are measured distributions, intervention effects and held-out predictions, with their uncertainty and controls.

Open questions.

(0) Forgetting and family heat capacity. At fixed finite \(N\), \(C_V\) does not diverge at one. On the positive-exponent family at \(N=2000\), the numerical maximum is approximately \(6.919812\) near \(g=1.256885\); the former threshold \(C_V{\gt}20\) is not an operative threshold in that setting. A slope change of \(0.05\) per epoch is also an unvalidated warning rule, especially when the estimator itself is context-dependent. No independent empirical corroboration of that proposed warning rule is established. Testing a warning rule requires matched checkpoints and predefined outcomes on held-out tasks, not coefficient or terminology matching.

(1) The initial panel has a Pythia-31M random estimate \(1.539824\); it does not support the former upper cap of \(1.35\). A cross-model empirical maximum would in any case depend on the acquisition protocol and selection of models.

(2) The EXP-D1 modular-addition pilot has 150 saved checkpoints. Its fitted gamma ranges from \(.319592\) to \(.456514\), always below one. Validation accuracy first exceeds \(.90\) at step 3400 and \(.95\) at step 3500; the latter threshold defines the reported grokking step, not a uniquely located transition. The probe uses four-token random sequences and only distances 1, 2 and 3, averaging different query pools at each distance. Three points do not establish an asymptotic attention tail. The saved field called \(C_V\) is actually \(1/|1-g|\) (with a cap), not the finite-family heat capacity. Thus the record does not support a crossing of one, but also does not identify an intra-phase circuit restructuring or settle a long-context grokking mechanism. The training model has learned absolute positions, not RoPE.

(3) Predicting forgetting from an inverse-coordinate score remains untested. (4) A relationship between vocabulary-rank and attention-distance exponents requires matched observables and controls; no exact duality is established.

L11: downstream validation remains restricted.

The saved cache and base-scaling experiments use WikiText-2 PPL and restricted numeric-key ranking. Neither validates multi-step reasoning, a universal cache exponent interval or an optimum for a target exponent. PPL measures predictive loss on the specified tokens, not coherence as an independent semantic outcome. Effects on math, code and long-document QA remain open; discarded attention mass alone does not predict their accuracy loss.

L12: no controlled MoE validation.

A saved OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 random-token E4 record does exist, so the former claim that no MoE profile was collected is incorrect. It is not a matched dense/MoE intervention study or an expert-conditioned analysis and does not validate a MoE extension of the horizon proposal.

L13: ALiBi bias is not the complete attention profile.

A linear negative-distance score bias contributes an exponential factor before normalization. Content scores, masks and numerical precision still matter. The historical BLOOM-1b7 zero at distance 5000 cannot by itself distinguish underflow, masking and very small positive mass. The exponentially cut-off family is a conditional mathematical model; its adequacy for ALiBi must be measured, not inferred solely from the position scheme.

L14: no established SGD-to-candidate attractor.

The constrained maximum-entropy result fixes a family after prescribing its log-distance moment; it does not determine which exponent SGD will learn. The rational-coordinate trajectory in Section 20 is not an observed optimizer trajectory. Neither a training attractor nor convergence to the configuration-based candidate follows from the saved pilot. The required dynamical bridge remains unproved.

L15: controlled-base pilot, instrument and training-objective audit.

The saved pilot contains three runs of a 4-layer GPT-NeoX-style transformer, with hidden size 128, four heads, head size 32, full rotary dimensions and 13,659,136 parameters. The code requests the same seed 42, initialization procedure, random-crop ordering and AdamW settings, while changing the base among \(10^4,10^5,10^6\). It sets both legacy and newer base configuration fields. No saved runtime frequency-buffer check or immutable library revision is available to certify their historical interpretation.

The script caps the WikiText-2 training stream at 2,000,000 tokens and requests 4000 steps of eight 512-token crops: 16,384,000 scheduled input-token presentations, with reuse. This is not one million training tokens or 2.4 million distinct corpus tokens. Nonfinite losses can skip steps and AMP can skip updates, so the schedule is not a verified optimizer-update count. The nine logged losses per run end at 6.466924, 6.475903 and 6.480629. These training losses are not held-out perplexities or convergence certificates.

Target-alignment defect in the saved script. Crops already set \(y_t=x_{t+1}\) and call the causal language model with labels=y. The standard causal loss shifts labels internally, pairing the logit at \(t\) with \(y_{t+1}=x_{t+2}\) instead of \(x_{t+1}\). Inspection of the installed Transformers 5.13.0 source and a synthetic-logit loss check verify this composition; no model forward pass is required. The historical runtime is not pinned, so this establishes a defect of the available recipe under that loss convention, not a reconstructed execution trace. The same internal shift also appears in the older public implementation. 2 The pilot cannot be certified as standard next-token pretraining without resolving this mismatch.

Measurement protocol. The extractor uses 30 crops for each distance \(d\in \{ 10,20,30,50,100,200,300,500\} \), with sequence length \(d+5\), all layers and heads, and the last query at distance \(d\). It reuses the training stream; lengths range from 15 to 505, rather than a fixed evaluation length 512. The candidate is nevertheless evaluated at \(T=512\). This is distinct from the earlier E4 protocol. The three per-base files match the combined JSON, and all slopes and fit scores below are replayed from eight saved means.

For uniform causal attention, the same selected entry equals \(1/(d+5)\). Fitting that null on the eight distances gives \(\widehat\gamma _0=0.9103752731\) and \(R^2=0.9978936065\). Consequently, a power fit above \(.99\) and a slope near one do not establish learned geometric organization. The excesses above this null are about \(.067\), \(.049\) and \(.049\); subtracting them does not isolate a causal exponent. The observed slopes fall from \(.9773\) to \(.9592\) and then rise slightly to \(.9596\), whereas the candidate rises from \(.9301\) to \(.9993\). In particular, the observed change from \(10^4\) to \(10^5\) has the opposite sign to \(\partial _\theta \gamma _P{\gt}0\) at fixed \(T\). This is a descriptive disagreement with the candidate’s direction, not a significance claim from this single-seed, instrument-confounded pilot. Relative errors of \(3.39\)–\(5.07\% \) are descriptive arithmetic, not a calibrated acceptance test or causal confirmation.

The stored records contain one seed, no per-crop dispersion, no untrained profile baseline and no held-out task validation. An “undertrained attractor” explanation is therefore untested. A useful future study would first correct target alignment, verify the runtime frequencies and estimator null, and then use matched seeds and held-out measurements. Simply extending the old recipe to more steps would not resolve these issues. Complete saved losses, means, scripts and displaced text remain in the evidence package; no new training or model inference is claimed by this audit.

L16: alternative explanations and measurement effects remain open.

The candidate alone is not an established sufficient explanation of the observed profiles. Corpus co-occurrence, optimization, learned query/key structure, masks and the estimator’s varying normalization are possible contributors. The uniform \(d+5\) null in L15 demonstrates that a substantial power-law slope can arise without learned distance preference. Their relative contributions require matched controls and cannot be identified by selecting the candidate from configuration alone. Earlier cross-model associations and the retained negative results remain descriptive evidence.

This atlas separates arithmetic/domain failures, saved observations and untested analogies. It does not assign a root cause where the experiment did not identify one. The compendium records current scope, not a list of universally working prescriptions.

19 Effective Coordinates and Dynamic Control Proposals

Existing interventions and the connection to Part III

The 5 November campaign records 8,064 interventions on 32 shared test prompts for Pythia-70M, Pythia-410M and GPT-2, including 1,152 zero-strength controls. For a 10% reduction of the attention output, the gradient predictor reduced MAE relative to the zero-effect predictor by 67.7%, 95.9% and 94.3%, respectively. These percentages concern prediction error, not model accuracy or capability. Full ablation is harder: Pythia-70M did not show a clear advantage over zero effect under the paired uncertainty analysis.

A discrepancy-selected follow-up comprises 18 cases, four step sizes and two precision variants (144 finite-difference records). The NeoX eager backend in Transformers 5.13.0 computes softmax in FP32 even with FP64 weights; the reference variant retaining FP64 softmax recovers convergence in the investigated cases. This is an exploratory numerical diagnosis, not an independent replication across all cases. The original backend and all campaign records remain preserved.

Part III uses these distinctions to separate an exact affine readout identity at a fixed final normalization from derivatives through the full sequence. A component’s direct write does not determine its downstream causal effect. The relevant saved-data revision is f240c0638bbfe8253a7e8098a4bc651b486ebabb of the TAF dataset.

19.1 Three proposed control surfaces

The measured head heterogeneity motivates experiments at more than one aggregation level. It does not give a learned model a unique global exponent or establish a Euclidean space of dimension \(1/\gamma \). A weight-threshold count alone neither defines a metric nor excludes Lorentzian or hyperbolic models. The previously introduced per-head metric component \(g_{vv}\) was not defined and is not used here.

Three proposals remain conceptually distinct from the historical hooks below:

  1. A per-token rule could compare a measured attention row to a target family using KL divergence. Computing that statistic costs \(O(N)\) per head/query once the row is available; extracting rows and changing rotary frequencies can incur additional costs and require cache consistency.

  2. A per-head rule could calibrate a different perturbation against each head’s actual profile, then test the resulting task effect. A target slope does not by itself determine an effective intervention.

  3. A per-task feedback rule could adapt a parameter using past-only statistics. Its stability, latency, stopping rule and held-out benefit need measurement. The training-time proposal in Section 12.3 does not establish these properties at inference.

No such KL-driven or slope-targeting controller is validated here. The November intervention-prediction campaign above is separate evidence with its own protocols and controls.

19.2 Historical hooks: implementation and causal validity

The saved experiments used Pythia-1B, requested fp16/eager attention and 50 WikiText-2 test chunks of length 1024, sampled with seed 42. The script resets that seed for each policy and reports the exponential of mean chunk loss. The JSON contains aggregate means and standard deviations, not paired per-chunk losses or immutable runtime revisions. The following source audit executes extracted hook definitions on synthetic tensors; it does not rerun the historical model or certify its exact library environment.

The attention-output cooler is not a causal per-head rule.

The hook attaches to the attention module output. In the inspected NeoX implementation that is after the output projection; reshaping its hidden coordinates into equal blocks does not recover the original head outputs. For each such block the code averages coordinate variance over the whole sequence, normalizes across blocks, and sets

\[ c_b=\max \{ 0,1-v_b/\overline v\} ,\qquad a_b=(1+\epsilon c_b)^{-1}. \]

It cools below-average spread, not the top 25% of heads. Neither \(v_b\) nor \(c_b\) is measured Fisher curvature or attention entropy.

Because the gate uses later positions, changing a suffix changes the gated output at an identical earlier prefix. Executing the original definition with two blocks of width two, \(\epsilon =.5\), and first vector \((1,-1,1,-1)\) gives first output \((.680203,-.680203,1,-1)\) when the second vector is \((1,-1,8,-8)\), but \((1,-1,.680203,-.680203)\) when it is \((8,-8,1,-1)\). The maximum prefix difference is \(.319797\); the zero-strength control returns its input exactly. Full-sequence teacher-forced scores with this gate therefore do not estimate an ordinary causal autoregressive perplexity. This structural failure is independent of whether a particular saved score improved or worsened. It does not quantify the size of leakage in that run.

The rotary hook also differs from its advertised intervention.

It multiplies both cosine and sine coordinates from index \(\lfloor .7D\rfloor \) onward. At \(D=64\) it changes coordinates 44–63, only part of one duplicated-frequency half, rather than complete rotary planes. With \(\epsilon =.5\), a changed coordinate has \(\cos ^2+\sin ^2=2.25\) instead of one. This is an anisotropic amplitude perturbation, not an orthogonal rotation, a base change or an established “dead-band” intervention.

19.3 Corrected implementation reference and its verified scope

New reference code is provided in corrected_reference.py. It repairs the implementation defects above without overwriting the historical code or reassigning its measured scores. The new rule is a per-query spread policy; it does not estimate entropy, Fisher curvature or a power-law exponent.

Let \(h_{b,t,a,r}\) be actual head outputs before the output projection, with batch \(b\), query \(t\), head \(a\) and coordinate \(r\). Rescale all coordinates and heads at each \((b,t)\) by their common maximum absolute value (using a positive floating-point floor at zero), obtaining \(u\). This common scaling prevents overflow and does not mix queries. The reference defines

\begin{align*} v_{b,t,a}& =\operatorname {Var}_{r}(u_{b,t,a,r}),\\ c_{b,t,a}& =\left[1-\frac{v_{b,t,a}}{\max (\operatorname {mean}_a v_{b,t,a},\tau )}\right]_0^1,\\ h’_{b,t,a,r}& =\frac{h_{b,t,a,r}}{1+\epsilon c_{b,t,a}}. \end{align*}

where variance uses the population denominator, \(\tau {\gt}0\) is a numerical floor and \(\epsilon \ge 0\). At \(\epsilon =0\) the input is returned exactly. The rule uses the current query’s head outputs only. Its factor lies in \([1/(1+\epsilon ),1]\); this amplitude statement is not a loss guarantee.

Proposition 19.1 Prefix causality of the corrected reference
#
📕 p. 87📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

Assume each upstream head output at query \(t\) depends only on input positions at or before \(t\). The displayed gate followed by a per-query output projection preserves that prefix causality. Because it uses no sequence aggregate or mutable state, partitioning the same head-output tensor into query chunks does not change the result.

Proof: in this note·Covers: not formalized·Cite: Proposition 19.1, p. 87, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

The variance, head mean, clipping and scaling at \((b,t)\) depend only on \(h_{b,t,:,:}\). Composing these functions and a per-query linear projection with the assumed causal upstream map cannot introduce a dependence on a later token. Chunk boundaries do not occur in their definitions.

💡 In plain words

If each head output at position \(t\) uses only the prefix up to \(t\), a gate computed per query and a projection also computed per query preserve that causality. Splitting the same tensor into query blocks does not change the computation. The proposition depends on the hypothesis about the preceding outputs; it does not by itself guarantee an improvement in loss or in attention.

Formal scope.

The paper gives the composition proof; this entry does not claim an Isabelle formalization of the program or of its empirical behaviour.

For the inspected NeoX layout, the adapter is a pre-hook on attention.dense, operating on its concatenated head input. It checks the declared head count and dimension. A general architecture requires its own verified concatenation and projection convention; attaching this adapter after a mixing projection would reintroduce the semantic error. The module does not automatically attach itself to other architectures.

The rotary reference builds angles from explicit positions and a vector of unique plane frequencies. It duplicates angles according to either split-half or interleaved pairing and computes their sine and cosine. Thus each pair has \(c_i^2+s_i^2=1\) and a norm-preserving \(2\times 2\) rotation; coordinates outside the declared rotary subspace are copied unchanged. These identities hold in exact arithmetic; floating-point checks use dtype-dependent tolerances, and an unrepresentable rotated output raises an error. A positive scale per plane changes angular frequency, not amplitude. No scale is claimed to detect dead bands, optimize context length or improve model performance.

Measurement, ablation and target alignment.

The same module includes three further corrections. Its distance-profile routine uses one explicit query set eligible at every fitted distance in a single attention tensor. On uniform causal attention its null is the constant mean \(|Q|^{-1}\sum _{q\in Q}1/(q+1)\); this is checked with distinct query lengths. It retains batch/head axes, rejects future attention and rejects distance-specific eligibility instead of silently changing the pool. The fused-NeoX ablation routine zeros complete declared rotary pairs of Q/K, leaving V and unrotated coordinates unchanged. It does not select those pairs using a semantic or dead-band classification.

The loss routine receives raw input IDs and aligns logits at \(t\) with the target at \(t+1\) exactly once. A valid-pair mask excludes padding at either position. It returns a sum of token losses and a valid-target count; corpus perplexity is \(\exp (\sum \mathrm{NLL}/\sum n)\), not an unweighted average of chunk means when counts differ. Nonfinite losses and empty target sets raise an error rather than being silently omitted. Logits are centered per row before evaluating the loss, avoiding cancellation from a large common offset; the final loss sum is also checked for overflow. The caller must supply raw IDs: matching shapes cannot detect an externally shifted sequence. These repaired routines do not reconstruct missing historical query sets, token losses or training runs.

The package records 145 implementation and arithmetic checks, including suffix substitution, prefix truncation, batch independence, token/chunk equivalence, a mixing-projection negative control, a synthetic causal-attention calculation, both rotary pairings, inverse rotations and partial-RoPE tails. Additional controls check single-shift targets, unequal chunk weighting, fixed-query nulls and complete-plane Q/K ablations without changes to V. Independent high-precision sums and quantiles check the numerical routines, including \(g=1\) and its neighborhood. Additional controls test large common logit offsets, loss-sum overflow and unrepresentable rotations. These are CPU tensor and formula tests; no pretrained model was loaded and no new trained-model PPL is asserted.

20 Rational Coordinates and the Limits of the RG Analogy

The rational candidate permits exact differentiation and iteration. These operations concern a scalar formula. No coarse-graining map on network states, Hamiltonian, measured critical exponents or universality class is established by them. The earlier identifications with Wilson–Fisher flow, Ising dynamics and a physical anomalous dimension are withdrawn. A separate percolation model for transformers trained on a formal languagepercolation2024emergence does not supply those missing identifications for this manuscript.

20.1 Candidate coordinate and legacy exponent definitions

For positive base and context, write

\begin{equation} g=\gamma _P=\frac{2\theta -T\sqrt2}{2\theta +T\sqrt2} =\frac{1-u}{1+u},\qquad u=\frac{T}{\theta \sqrt2}{\gt}0, \qquad -1{\lt}g{\lt}1.\tag {63} \end{equation}
71

Positive \(g\) additionally requires \(T{\lt}\theta \sqrt2\). This range belongs to the candidate, not to all measured attention slopes: several saved profiles exceed one. Calling \(g\) an anomalous dimension would require a separately defined observable and scaling law. It is not a consequence of RoPE.

The former critical-exponent list is retained as a set of definitions:

\begin{equation} \beta _{\rm leg}:=g-1,\qquad \nu _{\rm leg}:=(1-g)^{-1},\qquad \eta _{\rm leg}:=g-1,\quad g\ne 1.\tag {64} \end{equation}
72

These symbols are not independently measured order-parameter, correlation-length or anomalous exponents. The subscript distinguishes \(\beta _{\rm leg}\) from the differential-equation vector field below. For illustration, the rounded inputs \(g=.930,.674,.997\) give respectively \((\beta _{\rm leg},\nu _{\rm leg},\eta _{\rm leg})=\) \((-.070,14.286,-.070)\), \((-.326,3.067,-.326)\) and \((-.003,333.333,-.003)\). Divergence of this defined reciprocal at one does not imply divergence of the finite-family Fisher information.

20.2 Exact scalar trajectory and stability

At fixed \(\theta \), let \(\ell =\log u\). Direct differentiation gives

\begin{equation} \frac{dg}{d\ell }=\beta _{\rm flow}(g)=\frac{g^2-1}{2}. \tag {65} \end{equation}
73

With \(x=(1-g)/2\), this is the logistic equation

\begin{equation} \frac{dx}{d\ell }=x(1-x),\qquad 0{\lt}x{\lt}1.\tag {66} \end{equation}
74

It is a change of coordinates, not a derivation of training or layer dynamics. An antiderivative satisfying \(\beta _{\rm flow}=-V'\) is

\[ V(g)=\frac g2-\frac{g^3}{6}+C. \]

The old expression \(g-g^3/3\) has the wrong factor two for this same \(\ell \). This cubic is neither a quartic double-well potential nor a \(\mathbb Z_2\) symmetric potential. Evenness of the vector field does not make the flow invariant under \(g\mapsto -g\) with time orientation unchanged.

For \(g(\ell _0)=g_0\in (-1,1)\) the solution is

\begin{equation} g(\ell )=\tanh \! \left(\operatorname {arctanh}g_0 -\frac{\ell -\ell _0}{2}\right).\tag {67} \end{equation}
75

The derivative of the vector field is \(\beta '_{\rm flow}(g)=g\). Consequently \(+1\) is repelling and \(-1\) attracting for increasing \(\ell \). Neither endpoint is reached from the open interval at finite \(\ell \); initializing exactly at either endpoint gives a constant solution. The previous finite-time “birth point” and conflicting stability statements are therefore incorrect. Here \(\ell =\log (T/(\sqrt2\, \theta ))\) with fixed \(\theta \); it is not elapsed optimization time or the number of layers.

What the phase-gradient calculation actually checks.

For a rotary plane \(k\) in a subspace of dimension \(d_{\rm rot}\), \(\varphi _k(T,\theta )=T\theta ^{-2k/d_{\rm rot}}\) is smooth on \(T,\theta {\gt}0\). Defining \(A=d\varphi _k\) gives \(\partial _T A_\theta -\partial _\theta A_T=0\) because mixed derivatives commute. The one-form is globally exact on this domain, so its integral around a closed loop vanishes. No quantum state or Berry connection was defined. This calculation does not rule out memory or path dependence in trained network weights, and does not identify a Berry bundle of models.

Saved trajectory comparisons.

The historical size-axis exploration reports a best \(R^2\simeq .12\) for eight Pythia sizes under its proposed log-size/depth axes. The separate four-checkpoint sequence has global slopes \(.757234,.851255,.875856,.717686\) at steps \(1,1000,10000,143000\) (Table 30). It is nonmonotone, whereas the trajectory above is monotone on \((-1,1)\). The previously reported \(R^2=.15\) belongs to a fitted tanh template with free scale, not a direct confirmation of Eq. (67). These fit summaries are historical, not newly replicated training runs. Their poor fit does not identify a hidden data-dependent RG time. That identification would require a specified operation and independent tests.

20.3 Möbius map: correct domain and algebraic fixed point

Let \(M(z)=(2-z)/(2+z)\) for complex \(z\ne -2\). It satisfies

\[ |M(z)|{\lt}1\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \Re z{\gt}0, \]

since \(|2+z|^2-|2-z|^2=8\Re z\). Thus it maps the right half-plane to the unit disc. It does not map the upper half-plane to the disc: \(z=-1+i\) has \(M(z)=1-2i\) and \(|M(z)|^2=5\). The matrix \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\right)\) has determinant \(-4\); no real scalar multiple has determinant \(+1\). It is not an element of \(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb R)\) acting on the upper half-plane. Indeed \(\Im M(z)=-4\Im z/|z+2|^2\). The previous corrective note also went too far by denying every half-plane-to-disc interpretation; the right-half-plane statement is valid.

Solving \(M(z)=z\) gives the two roots \((-3\pm \sqrt{17})/2\) and hence

\begin{equation} z^*=\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{2}\simeq .561553.\tag {68} \end{equation}
76

At this positive root,

\[ M'(z^*)=-\frac{4}{(2+z^*)^2}\simeq -.609612. \]

The negative multiplier gives alternating local convergence. Global convergence from \(z_0{\gt}0\) follows by considering \(M^2(z)=(3z+2)/(z+6)\): it maps \([0,\infty )\) into \([1/3,3)\) and has derivative \(16/(z+6)^2\le 4/9\) there. Its unique positive fixed point is \(z^*\), so both subsequences converge. This is algebraic iteration; when \(z_0{\gt}2\), even its first iterate is negative and cannot be a positive context/base ratio. It is not a sequence of physical NTK interventions.

For the defined reciprocal \(\chi (g)=1/|1-g|\),

\begin{equation} \chi (z^*)=\frac{5+\sqrt{17}}4\simeq 2.280776. \tag {69} \end{equation}
77

This is the larger of the two positive roots of \(2y^2-5y+1=0\), not its unique positive root. It is an algebraic number, not an empirically established attention constant.

Why the 23-row clustering test is not informative.

The saved table computes \(z=T\sqrt2/\theta \) and Euclidean distance to \((\log z^*,z^*)\) in the \((\log z,\widehat\gamma )\) plane. Replaying all 23 rows gives \(0/23\) within radius \(.5\), but the smallest horizontal distance alone is \(.685814870\). Thus every row is outside the circle whatever its measured \(\widehat\gamma \). The former \(6.5\% \) rectangle-area reference does not condition on these chosen configurations; it cannot turn this structurally forced zero into evidence against a training attractor. No model trajectory under repeated transformations was measured. The full 23-row input is archived, without treating it as an independent replication or attributing within-family scatter uniquely to training data.

20.4 NIAH threshold proposal: not validated by the saved panel

The historical proposal combined the inverse coordinate with twice the mean needle distance:

\begin{equation} L_\mathrm {NIAH}^{\, c}=2d_{\rm inv}(\theta ,\gamma ) =\frac{2\theta (1-\gamma )\sqrt2}{1+\gamma }. \tag {70} \end{equation}
78

Substituting the candidate gives \(L^c=2T\) by construction. For the historical \(.748\) exponent, \(2d_{\rm inv}\) is about 4078, but v4 samples five lengths and does not locate a sharp threshold there. Its needles lie on a fixed depth grid; no per-trial curve survives in the JSON. Attention’s geometric dimension and a percolating support were not measured. The observed drop therefore certifies neither \(0.4\% \) threshold accuracy nor a universal retrieval ceiling. This proposal is separate from the formal-language percolation experiment cited above.

20.5 The norm-ratio score has no established packing interpretation

The audited \(M_{\rm hist}\) is a coordinate norm-ratio summary with a specified averaging order (Section 14.2). Equality to one denotes norm parity under that convention, not a reasoning/memory transition. No boundary, interior volume or semantic capacity has been defined. A controlled capacity experiment would need valid plane indexing, matched parameter budgets and held-out outcomes. NR-12 concerns soft decay and supplies no such test.

20.6 Fractional Laplacian: the missing operator assumptions

In one dimension the fractional Laplacian of order \(\alpha \in (0,2)\) uses a jump kernel proportional to \(|x-y|^{-1-\alpha }\), together with subtraction of function values and a prescribed domainkwasnicki2017. A formal match of tail powers would give

\begin{equation} s_{\rm formal}=\frac{\gamma -1}{2},\qquad \alpha _{\rm formal}=2s_{\rm formal}=\gamma -1. \tag {71} \end{equation}
79

The admissible range of this matching is \(1{\lt}\gamma {\lt}3\). For \(\gamma {\lt}1\) the index is negative and cannot describe an \(\alpha \)-stable diffusion; at one the index zero is outside the stated range. The Cauchy case is \(\alpha =1\) (formally \(\gamma =2\)), not \(\gamma =1\). The Brownian endpoint \(\alpha =2\) is a limiting local operator with Gaussian heat kernel, not an ordinary \(|x-y|^{-3}\) jump-density endpoint.

A row-stochastic attention matrix \(P\) preserves constants, \(P\mathbf1=\mathbf1\); a Laplacian annihilates them. The Markov generator is \(P-I\); with the positive-operator convention \((-\Delta )^{\alpha /2}\), a diffusion generator would have the opposite sign, \(-(-\Delta )^{\alpha /2}\). Identifying such a scaling limit still needs spatial homogeneity, tail, normalization, boundary and convergence assumptions. Content-dependent, finite, causal attention does not provide these automatically. The purpose-built fractional neural attention of qu2025fractional constructs its own diffusion mechanism; it does not establish the converse for ordinary softmax.

The attempted Green-function closure also fails.

Substituting \(s=(g-1)/2\) and \(d_{\rm eff}=1/g\) into the formal exponent \(2s-d_{\rm eff}\) gives \(g-1-1/g\). Equality with \(-g\) has roots \(g=1\) and \(g=-1/2\). Restricting to \(g{\gt}0\) leaves one, but at that point \(s=0\), outside the usual Riesz-kernel condition \(0{\lt}2s{\lt}d\). Even the positive algebraic root therefore supplies no physical Green-function identification. A threshold-count exponent is not a measured spatial dimension.

20.7 Conformal analogy: an exponent label is not a CFT

The rewriting

\begin{equation} d^{-g}=d^{-2h_{\rm formal}},\qquad h_{\rm formal}=g/2 \tag {72} \end{equation}
80

defines a label. It does not construct a primary operator, a state, conformal symmetry, an operator product expansion or Virasoro blocks. In two dimensions holomorphic weight and full scaling dimension also require a convention; one real distance exponent does not determine both weights. RoPE supplies particular frequencies, not exact scale invariance of learned attention. Exponential and other profiles are not excluded by this label.

Calabrese–Cardy’s logarithmic interval law concerns the von Neumann entropy of a reduced quantum state under specified CFT conditionscalabrese2004area_law. The present \(S_N\) is Shannon entropy of a distance distribution. Matching its leading logarithmic coefficient to \(c/3\) does not measure \(c=3\). The fixed-\(g{\lt}1\), \(g=1\) and fixed-\(g{\gt}1\) Shannon regimes also differ (Section 7.4). The proposed universal central charge, critical-exponent identification and higher-point predictions are withdrawn.

20.8 Conditional identities and their domains

The following are algebraic consequences of definitions, not independent tests on ten or more models:

  1. \((1/g)(g/2)=1/2\) for \(g\ne 0\). The threshold interpretation additionally uses \(g{\gt}0\); neither factor is a measured geometric or conformal dimension.

  2. \((g-1)/(1-g)=-1\) for \(g\ne 1\). This is not a demonstrated Widom hyperscaling law between independently defined observables.

  3. For \(-1{\lt}g{\lt}1\), the defined \(d_{\rm inv}\chi =\theta \sqrt2/(1+g)\) tends to \(\theta /\sqrt2\) as \(g\to 1^-\). The singular factors are not defined at one.

  4. Composing the inverse base with \(\gamma _P\) returns the target exactly. Remeasuring a changed model need not return that target. Thus the claimed empirical “NTK idempotency” is withdrawn.

For cross-reference, the algebraic fixed point is

\begin{equation} z^\star =\gamma _P(z^\star )=\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{2}. \tag {73} \end{equation}
81

It gives \(T/\theta =z^\star /\sqrt2\simeq .397078\), not \(.396\) exactly. Multiplying \(\theta \) by \(a{\gt}0\) at fixed \(T\) sends \(z\) to \(z/a\), not to \(M(z)\). Unless \(a=1\), it changes the candidate even at \(z^\star \). Iteration of \(M\) and repeated base scaling are different operations.

At fixed \(\theta \) the equivalent differential statement is

\begin{equation} \frac{dg}{d\log z}=\frac{g^2-1}{2}.\tag {74} \end{equation}
82

Its general interior solution has \(z(1+g)/(1-g)=C\); the particular candidate selects

\begin{equation} z\frac{1+\gamma _P(z)}{1-\gamma _P(z)}=2,\qquad z{\gt}0. \tag {75} \end{equation}
83

This is a coordinate identity. Substituting measured slopes does not make it an invariant under an actual network intervention, and its singular residual near \(g=1\) is not a calibrated physical error metric.

Finite zeta representation.

For integer \(N\ge 1\),

\[ Z_N(g)=\zeta (g)-\zeta (g,N+1),\qquad g\ne 1, \]

with analytic continuation where needed. The apparent poles cancel at one, yielding \(H_N\), not a finite-context divergence. For fixed \(g{\gt}1\) the infinite-support limit is \(\zeta (g)\). Values \(\pi ^2/6\) and \(\pi ^4/90\) belong to that limit at \(g=2,4\), respectively, not to a finite sum. Moreover positive \(\theta ,T\) constrain \(\gamma _P\) to \((-1,1)\); the inverse candidate cannot engineer those integer exponents.

Other proposed analogies.

The 39-curve Mittag–Leffler comparison historically reported a median ratio \(.23\) (standard deviation \(5.5\)) against \(1/\Gamma (1-g)\) and \(1.30\) (standard deviation \(.56\)) against a truncated-power normalizer. Each ratio would target one for its own exact normalization; \(1.30\) is not the predicted value of the first ratio. The quoted Pythia-2.8B residual sums \(.0068\) versus \(.0053\) favor the pure-power fit in that comparison. These heterogeneous profile summaries do not refute the mathematical Mittag–Leffler family or identify a waiting-time process.

Writing \(p(d)=|\psi (d)|^2\) with \(\psi \propto d^{-g/2}\) restates normalizability. Infinite-support summability changes at one; it is not an Anderson mobility edge without a Hamiltonian, disorder and eigenstates. Likewise inserting \(d_F=1/g\) in the proposed Flory expression gives \(3g/(1+2g)\) algebraically, but no polymer or time-dependent spreading law has been measured here. The historical values \(.861,.878,.976\) are substitution examples, not validated dynamical predictions.

The proposed BTZ horizon correspondence is also incorrect. In the usual uncharged rotating BTZ convention,

\[ r_-^2=\frac{M\ell ^2}{2} \left(1-\sqrt{1-\frac{J^2}{M^2\ell ^2}}\right) \]

for \(M{\gt}0\), \(\ell {\gt}0\) and \(|J|\le M\ell \)btz1992. It is not the written rational inverse-context formula. In particular \(J=0\) gives \(r_-=0\), whereas substituting \(g=0\) gives \(d_{\rm inv}=\theta \sqrt2{\gt}0\). No specified change of variables or charged solution repairs the asserted identification \(M=\theta \), \(g=Q/M\).

Finally, for \(g{\lt}1\) let \(C(g)=-\log (1-g)-g/(1-g)\). Along the scalar flow,

\[ \frac{dC}{d\ell }=\frac{g(1+g)}{2(1-g)}. \]

It is negative on \((-1,0)\) and positive on \((0,1)\). This is an elementary monotonicity calculation, not confirmation or violation of a CFT \(c\)-theorem, whose physical assumptions have not been supplied. At the chosen alpha-S gate center, setting its score to one similarly forces \(ND=e^2N_0D_0\) by normalization; it does not discover an induction constant.

20.9 Hallucination as horizon overshoot: an uncalibrated proposal

The original hypothesis related factual error to a candidate inverse coordinate. The proposal remains available for testing, but neither that coordinate nor the factor \(\chi =1/(1-\gamma )\) is an independently validated predictor of hallucination. In particular, the latter is not the finite-family Fisher information of Section 7.3.

Conjecture 20.1 Empirical hypothesis, not an established probability model
#
📕 p. 94📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

On a prespecified model and task panel, an inverse-coordinate score might be associated with factual-error frequency after controlling for context length, model and protocol. This association and its calibration remain untested here.

Cite: Conjecture 20.1, p. 94, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

💡 In plain words

The proposal is to test whether an inverse coordinate is associated with the frequency of factual errors on a panel and protocol fixed in advance.

Status.

It is a hypothesis with no proof and no empirical calibration here. The function \(s_{\rm hall}\) that follows the statement is a candidate score, not a probability of hallucination.

For \(\theta {\gt}0\), \(L{\gt}0\) and \(0{\lt}\gamma {\lt}1\), retain the candidate score

\begin{equation} s_{\rm hall}(L;\theta ,\gamma )= \max \{ 0,1-(d_{\rm inv}/L)^{1-\gamma }\} \, \frac{\sqrt\chi }{1+\sqrt\chi },\qquad \chi =\frac1{1-\gamma }. \tag {76} \end{equation}
84

Its earlier name \(P_{\rm hallucinate}\) suggested a calibrated probability, which has not been established. At \(L=2d_{\rm inv}\) the geometric factor is \(1-2^{\gamma -1}\): it equals \(0.292893\) at \(\gamma =0.5\) and \(0.066967\) at \(\gamma =0.9\), correcting the former value \(0.65\). As \(L/d_{\rm inv}\to \infty \) at fixed \(\gamma \), the score tends to \(\sqrt\chi /(1+\sqrt\chi )\). At \(L\le d_{\rm inv}\) it is zero by definition, not evidence of factual reliability or immunity to hallucination. The old Pythia and Yi numerical illustrations are preserved only in the separate predecessor archive; they are not measured error rates.

The related geometric hallucination index is also only a candidate score:

\begin{equation} \operatorname {GHI}(\theta ,\gamma ,L)= \max \{ 0,1-d_{\rm inv}/L\} \frac1{|1-\gamma |}, \qquad \theta ,L{\gt}0,\quad 0{\lt}\gamma {\lt}1. \tag {77} \end{equation}
85

It is not a probability, and extending it through \(\gamma =1\) or to a negative inverse length would require a new definition. Zero output does not imply zero risk. A test requires labelled outcomes, held-out calibration and comparison with simpler baselines on the same examples; TruthfulQA, FEVER or controlled cross-document tasks were proposed but were not evaluated for this formula. None of these definitions establishes two independent causal failure modes.

21.2 The five historical recipes and their current scope

X-1: cost comparison.

A cost comparison needs explicit prices, throughput, utilization and a tested quality target. The old alpha-S gate cannot decide whether training or self-hosting will meet that target (Appendix H). No present pricing or deployment recommendation is made here.

X-2: long-context viability.

The old composition of \(\gamma _P\), \(d_{\rm inv}\) and \(2d_{\rm inv}\) returns an algebraic length. It does not predict retrieval accuracy: \(d_{\rm inv}(\theta ,\gamma _P)=T\) by construction. Configuration-only retrieval verdicts and implied optimal base multipliers are withdrawn. Section 12 retains the saved task-specific comparisons and short-context costs.

X-3: training budget.

Parameter count and token budget are resource inputs. The assumed 400M cutoff and alpha-S score do not establish induction circuits or a training go/no-go criterion. A future estimator needs measured throughput and an independently specified quality objective.

X-5: hardware estimates.

The archived GPU catalogue and price/rate outputs are historical estimates. For a homogeneous cache, its basic storage is \(2BLNH_{\rm KV}d_{\rm head}b\) bytes, with batch \(B\), layers \(L\), retained positions \(N\), KV heads \(H_{\rm KV}\) and \(b\) bytes per scalar; real layouts can add padding, scales, metadata and allocation overhead. A hypothetical window can change \(N\), but \(D_f\) does not predict throughput or a safe compression ratio. Bandwidth, kernel implementation and measured quality are separate inputs. No USD/token or tokens/second ranking is certified.

X-19: cache mass and task outcomes.

The continuous quantile and exact discrete cumulative sum quantify mass conditional on the fitted family. Neither yields a universal PPL penalty. The configuration-only strategy ranking is withdrawn; compare actual policies with an uncompressed baseline on the intended workload and record KV head counts, precision, memory and timing.

21.3 Later mode catalogue and withdrawn diagnostic rules

The historical v0.4–v0.7 description claimed 22 modes, but the displayed list has 18 named rows plus Ask, Compare and Phase diagram: 21 named modes under that convention. Recipes and modes are overlapping interface concepts. No unexplained twenty-second mode is inferred or certified by this audit.

X-21: size-dependent imprint hypothesis.

The proposed formula was \(\gamma _{\rm random}=\gamma _P+\nu \log _{10}(P/(14\, \mathrm M))\), with \(\nu =-1/(2\pi )\). A rotation period does not derive that regression slope. The reported \(p=.022\) from a selected panel does not validate the fixed coefficient or identify anomalous training. The five-axis regression also used response-derived predictors (Section 5.5). Direct profiles with matched protocols are required; an error relative to this formula cannot diagnose a conversion or fine-tuning fault.

X-22: descriptive compute/context statistic.

The old \(K=\gamma \log (N^2D)\) used \(D=20N\) rather than each model’s observed training tokens. Its value depends on the counting units; an explicitly dimensionless version would need reference counts \(N_0,D_0\). The historical \(51.2\pm 16.8\) is a panel mean and spread, not an invariant or a calibrated anomaly threshold. The example \(K=74.6\) has \((74.6-51.2)/16.8=1.392857\) standard deviations, not established statistical outlier status. It is outside the quoted rounded one-spread band \([34,68]\); those two statements are compatible but do not imply a model defect.

X-23: corpus contrasts.

The old recipe used text-minus-random, opposite to the current \(\Delta \gamma =\widehat\gamma _{\rm random}-\widehat\gamma _{\rm text}\). Neither sign detects induction heads universally. The historical subgroup means \(-.19\) and \(+.03\) cannot be transferred between conventions or used as a substitute for circuit measurements and held-out ICL tests.

22 Conclusion

Coordinate and field audit.

The preserved B3 and amplification observations describe the implemented coordinate operations; their former frequency-specific causal interpretations are withdrawn. The field null reproduces a slope near the initial checkpoint, and spectral statistics require explicit basis and aggregation conventions. These are necessary corrections to the empirical interpretation, not new trained-model results. Matched plane interventions and fixed-context controls remain necessary before any mechanistic or deployment prescription.

Instrument control precedes physical interpretation.

The uniform-causal E4 control demonstrates that the measurement can produce a high-\(R^2\) apparent power law without learned attention. This weakens the initial-panel comparison as evidence for a geometric law. The fixed-query QL control does not share that slope confound on its audited fit range. Future model comparisons must preserve query sets, supports and null conventions; synthetic controls alone do not settle how much real-model behavior remains.

Attention-distance profiles provide useful empirical descriptions when their corpus, support and measurement protocol are stated. The finite power-law family supplies exact identities for normalization, entropy, Fisher information and a formal heat capacity. Maximum entropy selects that family under a prescribed log-distance moment and reference measure. Rotary geometry alone does not establish that trained attention solves this optimization problem.

The configuration-based Padé expression remains a candidate, not a universal prediction of the measured exponent. Its withdrawn derivation cannot be restored by algebraically inverting the same expression. The mixed initial comparison with 13 recorded bases has mean absolute exponent error \(0.167766\) and median absolute relative error \(19.2144\% \). The selected-case statistic is withdrawn because its membership and calculation could not be reconstructed. In the separate October replay, 25 of 42 historical identifiers have recovered measurements, and the stored candidate has rank correlation \(-0.445\) against 19 available QL fits. Protocol changes prevent interpreting those disagreements as a controlled estimate of one architectural or instrumental effect.

Compression and context experiments remain empirical observations under their recorded conditions. A family mass quantile does not guarantee autoregressive task accuracy, and an inverse-candidate base does not determine an optimal context-extension setting. The frozen-row output-error bound is useful within its fixed-score and fixed-value assumptions. The November intervention campaign provides a separate test of effect prediction on 32 shared prompts for three models; prediction gains do not establish improved model capability.

The next empirical steps are matched-protocol estimation with sequence uncertainty, prospective comparison against alternative profile families, and controlled task evaluation of proposed interventions. Circuit, geometric, physical and hallucination interpretations need evidence beyond exponent matching. Appendix K supplies eight verified groups that sharpen the mathematical part: null calibration, finite-grid and mixture bounds, quantile order, finite-family stability, truncation, softmax and a conditional cosine-to-power approximation. These results cover their stated hypotheses; they certify neither the empirical pipeline nor scientific novelty.

This edition integrates the November 12 full-document consistency review. The rational flow and map have corrected domains; physical identifications without the required structures are withdrawn. Adaptive historical controllers fail prefix causality, the fixed-point panel is uninformative by construction, and the V1/V2 comparison uses attention temperature in the context slot. The exact displaced arguments and complete predecessors are archived; Appendix J records their replacement; obsolete arguments are preserved outside the current manuscript. Historical provenance gaps and untested empirical hypotheses remain open. The audit is not a certificate that all scientific claims are error-free.

Code and data provenance.

The archived calculations and their limitations are described in Section 8. The companion project is github.com/karlesmarin/tafagent. This edition introduces no new model inference or software deployment. It incorporates the previously verified November 19 formal developments without modifying their proof sources. The source package includes the exact verified snapshot, its build and dependency receipts, a theorem-to-source map, and the manuscript integration and build checks.

A Symbolic Checks and Formal-Proof Scope

The historical SageMath scripts record symbolic explorations, not a blanket certificate of every displayed formula or interpretation. The accepted local Isabelle session from the earlier audit contains 20 scoped lemmas with quick-and-dirty disabled and no reported oracle dependencies. Its continuous variance lemma assumes the first two moments; it does not mechanize the integral. Its limitations remain unchanged by the new appendix. The earlier prior-art audit found eight direct own-repository precedents and one PDI precedent after reparametrization; novelty was not established for any of the twenty lemmas.

The eight-group extension is now presented in Appendix K, with its complete 300-fact Isabelle/HOL session and a map to the supplied proof sources. That development is separate from the earlier 20-lemma audit.

The corrected mathematical checks are:

  1. On continuous \([1,N]\), \(N{\gt}1\), the normalizer is \(Z_c=(N^{1-g}-1)/(1-g)\) with limit \(\log N\) at one. On discrete distances it is \(Z_N=\sum _{d=1}^N d^{-g}\) with value \(H_N\) at one.

  2. In the finite discrete family, \(U_N=-\partial _g\log Z_N\) and \(S_N=\log Z_N+gU_N\) are exact. The latter is Shannon entropy, not an entanglement or Cardy formula.

  3. \(I=\operatorname {Var}(\log d)\) and \(C_V=g^2I\) are finite for fixed \(N\). The value \((\log N)^2/12\) at one belongs to the continuous family.

  4. The continuous \(f\)-quantile is \([(1-f)+fN^{1-g}]^{1/(1-g)}\) with limit \(N^f\) at one. The large-\(N\) expression \(Nf^{1/(1-g)}\) requires fixed \(g{\lt}1\); it is not uniform near one and is not the exact discrete quantile.

  5. For \(N{\gt}1\), \(dU/dg=-I{\lt}0\) and \(dS/dg=-gI\), hence \(dS/dU=g\). The degenerate one-point family does not define this quotient.

  6. \(T\sqrt2/(1-\gamma _P)=\theta +T/\sqrt2\) is an exact composition with the linear inverse, not a first-order approximation to the Padé inverse.

The November 12 deep audit additionally invokes callable modules from Curiosity, Excovery, Socrates and Triangulum. It records module hashes, symbolic residuals, high-precision finite-sum checks, positive and negative controls, and candidate-span detection. Several tools share SymPy; agreement is not four independent proofs. Some parsers/checkers return inconclusive results, retained in the machine-readable evidence rather than promoted to certificates. Candidate extraction is not exhaustive semantic validation.

B Audit of the Attempted Geometric Derivation

The earlier “full proof” mixed an exact softmax identity with unproved statistical assumptions and inconsistent boundary conditions. Its full text is preserved in the predecessor source and replacement log. The steps below state precisely what survives and what fails.

Step 1: rotary scores and cycle counts.

With the actual rotary subspace \(d_{\rm rot}=2m\), a rotary score contains both cosine and sine coefficients: \(\sum _i[a_i\cos (d\omega _i)+b_i\sin (d\omega _i)]\), plus any unrotated contribution and the attention scaling factor. Completing one cycle at a particular distance does not average a sinusoid to zero. For fixed \(d\), averaging random inputs does not average the phase itself. Nor do independent token IDs establish zero-mean independent projected representations after learned transformations. Constant isotropic coefficients, a positive residual cosine mean and cancellation of cycled planes all require separate evidence.

If, as an extra hypothesis, the expected score were \(b+a\widetilde n_{\rm active}(d)\) in an unclipped log-linear range, its log-distance coefficient would be

\begin{equation} \kappa =\frac{am}{\log \theta }.\tag {78} \end{equation}
86

The earlier \(d_{\rm head}/(2\log \theta )\) omitted the coefficient \(a\) and equated the full head dimension to the rotary subspace. Even the correct conditional coefficient does not determine a learned exponent.

Step 2: averaging and the valid conditional theorem.

In general, \(\mathbb E[\operatorname {softmax}(s)]\ne \operatorname {softmax}(\mathbb E[s])\). Concentration of a denominator alone also does not replace \(\mathbb E[e^{s_d}]\) by \(e^{\mathbb E[s_d]}\). For example, with two logits \((X,0)\) where \(X=0\) or \(2\) equally often, the mean first softmax weight is approximately \(.690399\), whereas softmax of the mean logits gives \(.731059\). The interchange requires additional error control, not just a many-prompt average.

The valid statement is exact and conditional: if every logit on the chosen support has form \(s_d=c-g\log d\), then

\[ \operatorname {softmax}(s)_d =\frac{e^c d^{-g}}{\sum _{u=1}^N e^c u^{-g}}=\frac{d^{-g}}{Z_N(g)}. \]

This proves the consequence of a prescribed score profile. It does not derive that profile or \(g\) from a cycle-count geometry. The separate MaxEnt theorem likewise starts from a prescribed log-distance constraint.

Step 3: the rational candidate is not fixed by the old conditions.

For \(M_a(z)=(a-z)/(a+z)\), \(M_a(0)=1\) for every nonzero \(a\); this condition cannot select \(a=2\). The latter value gives \(M_2(1)=1/3\), not zero as previously claimed. Its zero occurs at \(z=2\), or \(T=\theta \sqrt2\), not \(T=\theta /\sqrt2\). At \(T=\theta \) it gives \((2-\sqrt2)/(2+\sqrt2)\simeq .171573\), not approximately one. One can obtain \(a=2\) by imposing the candidate derivative \(M_a'(0)=-1\), but that is a stipulated local condition; it still does not derive it from the measured attention process. The old error percentages on a selected “non-anomalous” subset neither repair these contradictions nor identify isotropy as the cause of all residuals. See the complete panels in Section 5.4.

Three distinct base mappings.

At a fixed positive \(T\), solving \(\gamma _P(\theta ,T)=g\) gives

\begin{equation} \theta _P(g,T)=\frac{T\sqrt2(1+g)}{2(1-g)},\quad -1{\lt}g{\lt}1. \tag {79} \end{equation}
87

The linear candidate instead has inverse \(\theta _L(g,T)=T\sqrt2/(1-g)\) for \(g{\lt}1\). Evaluating that different inverse on \(\gamma _P\) yields

\begin{equation} \theta _L(\gamma _P(\theta ,T),T)=\theta +\frac{T}{\sqrt2} =\theta (1+z/2),\qquad z=T\sqrt2/\theta . \tag {80} \end{equation}
88

The earlier Taylor expression used \(\theta (1+z)\) and was off by a factor two in its increment. No Taylor approximation is needed for the identity above. Finally the separate imposed relation \(g=\log \theta /\log b\) has inverse \(b=\exp (\log \theta /g)\) for \(g\ne 0\); it is neither of the other two inverses. At \(\theta =10000,T=1000\), the Padé inverse returns 10000 exactly and the linear composition gives 10707.106781. Their difference is \(7.071068\% \) of 10000, not a sub-\(0.5\% \) inverse error. At \(T=5000\) it is \(35.355339\% \), not below \(2\% \).

Integer \(N\ge 1\), real \(\gamma \), counting measure.

Log moment

\(U_N=\sum _d p_\gamma (d)\log d\)

Equals \(-\partial _\gamma \log Z_N\).

Entropy

\(S_N=\log Z_N+\gamma U_N\)

Exact finite-sum Shannon entropy; \(0\le S_N\le \log N\).

Fisher metric

\(I(\gamma )=\operatorname {Var}_{p_\gamma }(\log d)\)

Finite at every real \(\gamma \) for fixed \(N\); evaluate directly at zero.

Formal heat capacity

\(C_V=\gamma ^2I(\gamma )\)

Family susceptibility, not an identified task sensitivity.

Intrinsic length

\(\left|\int _{g_1}^{g_2}\sqrt{I(g)}\, dg\right|\)

Distance along this statistical family.

Continuous normalizer

\(Z_c=(N^{1-\gamma }-1)/(1-\gamma )\); \(Z_c(1)=\log N\)

Lebesgue measure on \([1,N]\), \(N{\gt}1\); not the discrete normalizer.

Variance at one

\(C_{V,c}(1)=(\log N)^2/12\)

Continuous only. For discrete distances use the variance of \(\log d\).

Free-energy coordinate

\(-\log Z_N\)

Dimensionless coordinate; division by \(\gamma \) gives the thermal convention for \(\gamma \ne 0\).

Discrete mass window

\(\min \{ k:\sum _{d=1}^k d^{-\gamma }\ge fZ_N\} \)

Integer distance quantile; \(0{\lt}f{\lt}1\).

Continuous mass window

\([(1-f)+fN^{1-\gamma }]^{1/(1-\gamma )}\); \(N^f\) at \(\gamma =1\)

Quantile of the continuous family, not an accuracy bound.

Padé candidate

\((2\theta -T\sqrt2)/(2\theta +T\sqrt2)\)

\(\theta ,T{\gt}0\); range \((-1,1)\); empirical identification unestablished.

Inverse base

\(T\sqrt2(1+g)/(2(1-g))\)

\(-1{\lt}g{\lt}1\), \(T{\gt}0\); candidate inversion, not a task optimum.

Inverse context

\(d_{\rm inv}=\theta \sqrt2(1-g)/(1+g)\)

\(-1{\lt}g{\lt}1\), \(\theta {\gt}0\); not a validated retrieval ceiling.

Shifted base

\(b(T)=\theta +T/\sqrt2\)

Exact coordinate definition; different from the inverse base.

Log base ratio

\(\log [b(D)/b(N)]\)

Signed coordinate change, not established information loss.

Threshold exponent

\(d_{\rm eff}=1/\gamma \), \(\gamma {\gt}0\)

Records a weight-threshold count exponent, not measured geometric dimension.

Effective support

\(\exp S_N\)

Entropy effective number within the chosen family, not a task context limit.

Frozen-row bound

\(\| o-o_K\| \le \epsilon \, \operatorname {diam}\{ v_j\} \)

Fixed scores and values, renormalized retained row, removed mass \(0\le \epsilon {\lt}1\).

Soft decay

\(w(d)=(1-d/d_{\rm inv})^\gamma \) inside \(0{\lt}d{\lt}d_{\rm inv}\)

For positive \(\gamma ,d_{\rm inv}\): use \(\log w\) as a score bias; an empirical proposal, not a geometry theorem.

Corpus contrast

\(\widehat\gamma _{\rm random}-\widehat\gamma _{\rm text}\)

Matched-protocol descriptive statistic; not a causal architecture identifier.

Colour: green = yes / holds.

Asymptotic entropy is a separate statement.

For fixed \(0{\lt}\gamma {\lt}1\),

\[ S_\gamma (N)=\log N-\log (1-\gamma )-\frac{\gamma }{1-\gamma } +O(N^{\gamma -1}\log N). \]

At one it is \(\tfrac 12\log N+\log \log N+O(1)\); above one it converges to \(\log \zeta (\gamma )-\gamma \zeta '(\gamma )/\zeta (\gamma )\) for fixed \(\gamma {\gt}1\). These regimes cannot be merged into the former \((1-\gamma )\log N\) expression.

D Zipf and Attention: Saved-Panel Audit

For two members of the same finite power-law family with integer \(N{\gt}1\), equality of log moments identifies equal exponents on the same support and reference measure (Section 6.3). Equal moments of arbitrary distributions do not imply this conclusion. Vocabulary ranks and token distances are different observables. The saved Zipf file contains eight attempted entries: seven successful estimates and one gated-access failure for Gemma. Replaying the seven pairs gives Pearson \(r=-.505314\); this is a valid descriptive cross-row statistic, not an undefined constant-vector calculation.

E Quick Reference Card

Purpose. Separate measurement, family calculations and intervention tests. The original configuration-only deployment card is preserved only in the separate predecessor archive indexed by Appendix J.

1. Define and measure the observable.

Record immutable model and tokenizer revisions where available, corpus snapshot, precision, attention backend, query selection, distance support, bins and aggregation. Fit the declared profile and report sequence-level uncertainty. A large \(R^2\) alone does not identify an architecture or certify a power law. Compare alternative families on the same observations and loss.

2. State which exponent is being used.

Use \(\widehat\gamma \) for a measured fit and \(\gamma \) for a family parameter. The configuration candidate \(\gamma _P=(2\theta -T\sqrt2)/(2\theta +T\sqrt2)\) lies in \((-1,1)\) for positive inputs and cannot stand in for every observed exponent. Use the explicitly identified comparison panels in Section 5.4, not the withdrawn selected-case accuracy claim. Corpus contrasts require a matched protocol and do not alone identify circuits.

3. Compute the appropriate mass window.

For integer token distances use

\[ D_{f,N}=\min \left\{ k:\sum _{d=1}^{k}d^{-\gamma }\ge fZ_N(\gamma )\right\} . \]

For the distinct continuous density on \([1,N]\), use

\[ D_{f,c}=\begin{cases} [(1-f)+fN^{1-\gamma }]^{1/(1-\gamma )},& \gamma \ne 1,\\ N^f,& \gamma =1. \end{cases} \]

State \(N{\gt}1\) and \(0{\lt}f{\lt}1\). These are mass quantiles under a chosen family, not measured memory savings or guarantees about accuracy.

4. Interpret inverse Padé as algebra.

For \(-1{\lt}g{\lt}1\) and \(T{\gt}0\),

\[ \theta _{\rm inv}=\frac{T\sqrt2(1+g)}{2(1-g)},\qquad \alpha _{\rm cand}=\frac{\theta _{\rm inv}}{\theta _{\rm nominal}}. \]

No task optimum follows. Substituting the candidate into its context inverse returns \(T\) identically and cannot independently validate a retrieval horizon. The exponential and linear legacy inverses are different functions.

5. Evaluate the intervention.

Use held-out paired examples to measure perplexity or task quality together with actual resource savings. Include the unchanged model and relevant baselines. Keep missing measurements distinct from zero outcomes. Report the scope of uncertainty and failure cases. An anomaly score suggests a hypothesis; causal circuit identification requires additional interventions.

F Productive Negative Results

Revision of 7 November 2026

The negative-result record is retained in full. Numerical results retain their original protocol and provenance limits; their preservation is not a fresh replication. A failed physical analogy does not establish a replacement physical theory. The corrected baseline and instrument distinctions apply to positive and negative outcomes alike.

The historical identifiers below are retained, including the original jump from NR-10 to NR-12; no NR-11 result is supplied. They are not nine independent replications. A failed candidate, a weak correlation and an uninformative experiment have different meanings. None establishes a replacement law or an inference-time invariance of learned attention.

NR-1: a poor beta-family parameterization.

The historical 14-model symbolic regression reports \(R^2=.052\) for the chosen geometric parameterization. This does not rule out all beta distributions or prove that power and exponential families exhaust the alternatives. MaxEnt uniqueness holds under its stated constraint; a failed regression is not an additional uniqueness proof.

NR-2: nonconstant radius/training-length ratio.

The historical 14-model coefficient of variation \(.885\) describes the selected ratios \(D_{.9}/T_{\rm train}\). It does not establish any universal replacement invariant, nor derive the empirical scatter from \(\gamma _P\).

NR-3: H3 applicability was not quantified by the proposed bound.

The legacy account mixes short/long distances 50/100 with a later assertion about distance 1000, and reports nonpositive log-probability differences for its tested RoPE models. These protocol settings cannot be reconciled from that prose alone. The continuous zero-count scale \(2\pi \theta \) is not an identified degradation threshold, and the proposed ratio \(n_{\rm dead}(d_{\rm long})/N{\gt}1.5\) has no validated applicability theorem. The observed contrasts do not establish the claimed root cause; a recoverable protocol, a nondegenerate baseline contrast and controlled patching are needed.

NR-4: Attention-entropy proxy (\(|r| \le 0.23\)).

We hypothesised that per-layer attention entropy \(H_\mathrm {attn}(\ell )\) is an inverse proxy for the H3 recovery ratio \(R(\ell )\): when the model cannot recover (\(R=0\)), attention should be uniform (\(H_\mathrm {attn} \approx \ln T\)); when recovery is complete (\(R=1\)), attention should be concentrated (\(H_\mathrm {attn} \approx 0\)). NR-6/7/8 — Three inference-time perturbation records.

Three experiments attempted to manipulate \(\gamma \) at inference time:

(a) Temperature sweep (\(\tau \in [0.3, 2.0]\), pythia-70m, 4-bit weights, bf16 compute, random-token lengths \(d+200\), query \(d+199\) and key 199, matching the protocol of (b), \(N = 30\) prompts): fitting \(\gamma (\tau ) = \gamma _0\, \tau ^{-\beta }\) gives \(\beta = -0.008\), \(R^2 = 0.014\)—no monotonic trend. The replayed minimum is \(.674860\), maximum \(.757621\), and full range \(.082761\). The largest absolute change from the \(\tau =1\) baseline \(.749359\) is \(.074499\); the range is not a symmetric \(\pm .083\) interval. The eight stored means at \(\tau =1\) are exactly identical to the eight means at base 10000 in (b), not merely equal after rounding. Both scripts reset the same random generator and use the same extraction. This explains the shared baseline at the data level; without run identifiers it does not establish whether it was acquired once or twice. It is not independent replication evidence. Softmax is invariant to adding a common scalar, not to scaling logits. This recorded slope stability does not establish invariance of the attention matrix.

(b) Inference-time base sweep. The nine Pythia-70M settings use 4-bit weights with bfloat16 compute, 30 random-token prompts per distance, all heads/layers and lengths \(d+200\). The saved helper patches the actual partial-rotary inverse-frequency buffers and their original copies. No weights are retrained. All nine fits replay from the saved eight-distance means. Their range is \(.478980\)–\(.772036\) (width \(.293056\)), not \(\le .08\); the largest departure from the nominal-base fit \(.749359\) is \(.270379\). The weakest power fit has \(R^2=.610621\) at base 4000. The regression of observed on candidate slopes remains \(.152860\) with \(R^2=.144304\). The matched uniform-attention null is \(.439001\) for this \(d+200\) instrument. These observations contradict faithful candidate tracking but establish neither invariance to base changes nor a mechanism in which weights encode the training base. The complete panel is retained below.

NR-9 — The spectral scaling claim depends on the instrument.

The old Pythia-1B head-dimension correction changed the reported reciprocal ratio from about \(1.38\) to \(1.111\), but did not repair full-head grouping, rotary pairing or the aggregation ambiguity. Replaying the five saved Pythia records gives a strong sample correlation \(r=-0.986580\) for the reciprocal ratio with head dimension and \(r=+0.987556\) for \(M_{\rm hist}\). These are ordinary Pearson correlations over five confounded sizes, not causal laws or partial correlations. The field-dispersion statistic has its own context-length null and missing-data rule (Section 14.3). The episode supports instrument auditing, not a claim of no architectural effect or a validated semantic score.

NR-10 — Coordinate-pruning costs do not validate a layer boundary.

Section 11.7 preserves the v1 and complete v2 records, their evaluation settings and the exact regression conventions. The available script’s selected high-index output coordinates are outside the rotary subspace in the audited Pythia-1B and 2.8B configurations. The observation is therefore a coordinate ablation, not established removal of alive RoPE bands. For a selected data set \(S\), the descriptive model is

\begin{equation} y_i=a_S+b_Sx_i+e_i,\qquad x_i=100\, \mathrm{frac}_{Q/K,i},\quad y_i=\Delta \mathrm{PPL}_i. \tag {81} \end{equation}
91

The original common coefficient \(0.175\pm 0.005\) and \(r{\gt}0.99\) claims are withdrawn. The v2 positive-point slopes are \(0.189964\) (1B, three points) and \(0.313581\) (2.8B, four points); through-origin slopes are \(0.153883\) and \(0.167242\). The two-point 1B v1 fit is another subset. Small positive cost at one layer does not establish a harmless pruning boundary; increasing the intervention produces larger recorded costs. It also does not turn an entropy identity into a pruning prescription.

NR-12 — The three-model soft-decay comparison has no validated boundary.

The full four-policy table is in Section 11.6. Baseline has the smallest recorded PPL for 2.8B, soft decay for 1.4B and hard \(D_f\) for 1B. The former proposed rule is retained only as an unvalidated hypothesis:

\begin{equation} h\gtrsim T_{\rm train}/2 \quad \text{(historical cutoff heuristic, not an iff criterion).} \tag {82} \end{equation}
92

The 2.8B improvement relative to hard-cutoff PPL is \(1.155\% \); \(20.729\% \) uses the excess over baseline as denominator. Hard truncation at precisely \(T_{\rm train}\) was not tested in this panel, nor were equal retained mass or a causal smoothness mechanism established. The no-op and failed cases remain part of the record. Per-chunk outcomes are needed for paired uncertainty.

NR-13: the V1/V2 comparison has a context-input error.

The saved twenty-row comparison defines \(g_{V2}=g_{V1}(1-\log 2/d_{\rm head})\). Recomputing its relative-error columns reproduces mean errors \(30.112029\% \to 29.780277\% \), median errors \(15.463669\% \to 15.997564\% \), and 13/20 row wins for V2. Thus mean error improves slightly while median error worsens; “no MAE improvement” was incorrect. The Pythia-only \(d_{\rm head}\le 80\) subset contains six rows, not four.

More fundamentally, all stored V1 values reproduce the rational formula when its context slot is filled by the corresponding master record’s T_attn, to numerical precision. That field is the rounded attention-temperature coordinate near \(1/g_{\rm obs}\), not an evaluation context length. For example, Pythia-1B uses \(T=1.0740\), yielding \(g_{V1}=.999848125\), instead of a token context such as 2000. This both confuses observables and feeds a response-derived coordinate into the prediction. The generator of this validation file was not reconstructed, but the exact stored-value match identifies the input mismatch independently. The frozen twenty rows and master record are included in the audit package.

Consequently this panel cannot validate or reject a finite-head correction at the intended contexts, establish residual causes, or make V1 canonical. The alleged continuum derivation is already withdrawn (Appendix B). A new comparison needs actual context inputs, valid rotary dimensions, prespecified fitting populations and an independent outcome; the old five-axis response-leaking fit supplies none.

App. F

H The Historical Alpha-S Gate: Definition and Failure

This appendix defines the proposed score and recalculates all four examples from their declared inputs. The original table remains in the separate archive. Its semantic-ignition interpretation and pre-training go/no-go rules are withdrawn. The scale \(N_0=4\times 10^8\) is an assumption, not an induction-head threshold from olsson2022induction; their evidence includes two-layer attention-only models. The symbol \(N_{\rm IH}\) in the historical equations below denotes that assumed reference only.

H.1 Retained definition

\begin{equation} \boxed {\; \alpha _S \; =\; F_{R_c} \cdot F_\mathrm {Chin}\; } \tag {83} \end{equation}
93

where the two factors are:

\begin{align} F_{R_c} & \; =\; \tfrac {1}{2}\bigl(1 + \tanh \! \bigl(3(R_c - R_c^\star )\bigr)\bigr), \qquad R_c^\star \approx 1.68 \\ & \quad \text{(provisional, $n{=}4$; see caveat below and \S 16.4)}, \\ F_\mathrm {Chin} & \; =\; \log \! \frac{N_\mathrm {params}\cdot D_\mathrm {tokens}}{N_\mathrm {IH}\cdot D_\mathrm {IH}}, \qquad N_\mathrm {IH} = 4\! \times \! 10^{8},\; \; D_\mathrm {IH} = 2\! \times \! 10^{11}. \end{align}

The coefficient 3, centre 1.68 and token scale \(2\times 10^{11}\) were heuristic choices. The logarithmic factor is not a derivation of compute-optimal training or a probability of circuit formation; it can be negative below its chosen product reference. No Hagedorn susceptibility appears in the actual definition. The factorization does not establish a Chinchilla–Hagedorn unification.
