H.3 Why the design rule is withdrawn

The nine-model ratio audit in Section 16.4 supplies counterexamples to the proposed monotone gate. Its range-hull intersection is \([0.924358,3.085057]\), not a calibrated uncertainty region. The formerly cited Pythia-2.8B “observed post-IH” failure also mixes protocols: the round-3 summary has positive contrast \(+0.041\), whereas another corpus comparison has a different sign. Neither establishes a unique induction label.

The proposed alternative \(\alpha _S^{\rm v2}=F_{\rm Chin} [1+c\tanh (3(R_c-R_c^\star ))]\) was a new hypothesis, not a validated repair. Retuning a score after observing failures requires separate evaluation on held-out data with direct outcomes. No architecture, budget or training decision should use either gate as evidence that induction or retrieval will emerge.

🛡️ Evidence & scope

No correction can reconstruct unrecorded observations or immutable runtime revisions. K Eight Formally Verified Result Groups

This appendix integrates the eight groups of the November 19 technical note into the manuscript. Each statement below has explicit hypotheses and a readable proof; the accompanying Isabelle/HOL sources supply the machine-checked derivations. The complete session audited 300 named facts from the project’s theories. This is a count of intermediate and final facts, not 300 independent theorems. The eight auxiliary Lean lemmas have a narrower scope. The results establish mathematical implications, not that a trained model satisfies their premises. No new model measurements are introduced.

Conventions.

All logarithms are natural. Probability supports are finite and nonempty unless a continuous integral is explicitly displayed. We use \(\operatorname {TV}(p,q)=\frac12\sum _j|p_j-q_j|\) and the usual extended-real KL divergence, with zero-mass terms omitted and a positive mass divided by zero giving \(+\infty \). The real exponent \(g\) denotes the same family parameter as \(\gamma \) elsewhere; it is distinct from an observed regression slope. For finite values \(v_j\) in a real normed vector space, \(\operatorname {diam}\{ v_j\} =\max _{i,j}\| v_i-v_j\| \).

K.1 Group 1: the instrument null and logarithmic calibration

Fix distances \(d_k{\gt}0\), \(x_k=\log d_k\), positive regression weights \(w_k\) with \(\sum _k w_k=1\), and \(V_x=\operatorname {Var}_w(x){\gt}0\). For any positive profile \(A\), including a fitted intercept, define

\begin{equation} G_w(A)=-\frac{\operatorname {Cov}_w(x,\log A)}{V_x}. \tag {87} \end{equation}
97

The points and weights are held fixed when two slopes are compared.

Theorem K.1 General uniform null and exact calibration
#
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

At distance \(d_k\), a probe averages allowed attention entries using weights \(\alpha _{kr}\ge 0\), \(\sum _r\alpha _{kr}=1\). If row \(r\) has \(n_{kr}\ge 1\) allowed keys, its uniform-attention null is

\[ A_{0,k}=\sum _r\frac{\alpha _{kr}}{n_{kr}},\qquad G_w(A_0)=-\frac{\operatorname {Cov}_w(x,\log A_0)}{V_x}. \]

For every positive profile on the same grid and regression weights,

\begin{equation} G_w(A/A_0)=G_w(A)-G_w(A_0). \end{equation}
98

A constant null has zero slope. Keeping the same queries, support sizes and averaging weights at each distance is sufficient for a constant null.

Isabelle · ours · partshow

Only a part is in Isabelle: Requires fixed probe weights and a finite probability; it does not characterize learning.

    and n: "\<And>k r. k\<in>K \<Longrightarrow> r\<in>R \<Longrightarrow> n k r = m r"
    and k: "k\<in>K"
  shows "probe_null R a n k = (\<Sum>r\<in>R. b r / real (m r))"

    and pos0: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> 0 < A0 i"

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: part: Requires fixed probe weights and a finite probability; it does not characterize learning.·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

🆕 Classical and new: Application to the measurement protocol; the elementary identities are not presented as new.

↳ Used in: Theorem K.2, Theorem K.3

Proof ▼

An allowed entry in a uniform row equals \(1/n_{kr}\). Averaging gives the displayed null, which is positive. Substitute \(\log (A_k/A_{0,k})=\log A_k-\log A_{0,k}\) in Equation (87); covariance is linear in its second argument. The covariance with a constant is zero.

💡 In plain words

The measured slope depends on the probe and on the regression weights. A uniform row can produce an apparent profile; subtracting the slope of a null built with the same instrument cancels that contribution algebraically. The proof does not describe how a trained model behaves.

Fixed queries and complete diagonals.

For a fixed causal context \(T\), zero-based query indices \(i\in Q\) and fixed weights \(\alpha _i\), suppose every fitted distance is eligible for every query. Then \(A_{0,\mathrm{QL}}(d)=\sum _{i\in Q}\alpha _i/(i+1)\) is constant. By contrast, averaging every entry of the causal diagonal gives

\[ A_{0,\mathrm{ALL}}(d)=\frac{1}{T-d}\sum _{i=d}^{T-1}\frac{1}{i+1}, \qquad d\in \{ 1,\ldots ,T-1\} . \]

This null strictly decreases between successive eligible distances: removing the largest member of the strictly decreasing sequence \(1/(d+1),\ldots ,1/T\) decreases its mean. Thus its OLS exponent is positive on any grid with at least two distinct distances and positive weights. The pairwise covariance identity in Group 2 proves the strict sign.

Scope and counterexamples.

The subtraction is a slope relative to a declared null, not a proof of unbiased estimation or causal attribution. Binning, exclusions and weights must be reproduced in the control; averaging and logarithms do not commute. Fixed queries are sufficient, not necessary: a row with six allowed keys and an equal-weight average of rows with four and twelve allowed keys both give \(1/6\). Also, zero covariance on a grid need not imply a constant profile. For dot-product attention without a key-dependent additive bias, setting the query projection to zero leaves every rotary query zero and gives a uniform softmax. A fixed-query probe then has zero exponent for any RoPE base. This refutes a nonzero geometry-only law over all possible weights; it does not characterize a specified training procedure.

K.2 Group 2: finite-grid bounds for affine exposure

The secant identity.

For the weights above and real observations \(y_k\),

\[ \operatorname {Cov}_w(x,y)=\sum _{i{\lt}j}w_iw_j(x_j-x_i)(y_j-y_i),\qquad V_x=\sum _{i{\lt}j}w_iw_j(x_j-x_i)^2. \]

Expanding the corresponding half-sum over all ordered pairs proves both identities. Hence the regression slope is a convex combination of secants over pairs with distinct \(x\) values, with weights \(w_iw_j(x_j-x_i)^2/V_x\).

Theorem K.2 Affine-exposure bias
#

Uses

  • Theorem K.1
  • Theorem K.1
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

For \(A_0(d)=c/(ad+b)\) with \(a,b,c{\gt}0\), on the nondegenerate grid of Group 1,

\begin{equation} \frac{ad_{\min }}{ad_{\min }+b}{\lt}G_w(A_0){\lt} \frac{ad_{\max }}{ad_{\max }+b}. \end{equation}
99

With the grid and weights fixed, this slope strictly decreases with \(b\). Replacing all distances by \(\lambda d_k\), \(\lambda {\gt}0\), makes the slope strictly increase with \(\lambda \); its limits as \(\lambda \downarrow 0\) and \(\lambda \to \infty \) are respectively zero and one. The amplitude \(c\) has no effect.

    and range: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> l\<le>x i" "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> x i\<le>u"
  shows "a*exp l/(a*exp l+b)<fw_cov S p x (\<lambda>i. affine_log a b (x i))/fw_var S p x"

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: part: Describes the bias of the instrument under affine exposure; not a mechanism of the transformer.·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

The slope is the regression of \(f(x)=\log (ae^x+b)\) on \(x\). Its derivative \(ae^x/(ae^x+b)\) strictly increases. The mean-value theorem places each nontrivial secant strictly between the endpoint derivatives; the convex combination proves the bounds. Differentiating the finite covariance gives

\[ \partial _bG_w=\frac{\operatorname {Cov}_w(x,1/(ae^x+b))}{V_x}{\lt}0, \qquad \partial _\lambda G_w= \frac{\operatorname {Cov}_w(x,ad/(a\lambda d+b))}{V_x}{\gt}0. \]

The signs follow from the pairwise identity and strict opposite or common ordering. Adding \(\log \lambda \) to every \(x_k\) changes neither centered coordinates nor variance. On a finite grid, the log-profile tends to a constant at zero scale, while \(\log (a\lambda d+b)=\log (a\lambda )+\log d+o(1)\) at infinite scale. Constants disappear from the covariance, including \(\log c\).

💡 In plain words

If the number of exposed positions has the form \(ad+b\), the local elasticity is a fraction between zero and one. The OLS slope lies between the extreme values of that elasticity on the grid. Changing the grid or the offset changes the instrument’s reading.

For the initial E4 null, \(a=1,b=50\). Its scale-dependent slope is therefore present without learning. The boundary cases, outside the strict hypotheses, give slope one for \(b=0,a{\gt}0\), and zero for \(a=0,b{\gt}0\).

K.3 Group 3: mixing profiles changes slope and curvature

Theorem K.3✅ Isabelle Positive mixtures of powers
#

Uses

  • Theorem K.1
  • Theorem K.1
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

Let \(J\ge 1\), \(a_j{\gt}0\), \(g_j\in \mathbb R\), and \(A(d)=\sum _{j=1}^{J}a_jd^{-g_j}\) for \(d{\gt}0\), with coefficients and exponents independent of distance. For \(x=\log d\), put \(\pi _j(x)=a_je^{-g_jx}/\sum _\ell a_\ell e^{-g_\ell x}\). Then

\begin{align} g_{\rm loc}(x)& =-\frac{d}{dx}\log A(e^x)=\sum _j\pi _j(x)g_j, & g_{\rm loc}’(x)& =-\operatorname {Var}_{\pi (x)}(g)\le 0. \end{align}

The finite-grid exponent satisfies

\[ \min _j g_j\le g_{\rm loc}(x_{\max })\le G_w(A) \le g_{\rm loc}(x_{\min })\le \max _jg_j. \]

If two component exponents differ, the local slope strictly decreases, and the mixture cannot be an exact power on any open interval.

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: the whole statement·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

Logarithmic differentiation yields the weighted mean. Since \(\pi _j'=\pi _j(-g_j+\sum _\ell \pi _\ell g_\ell )\), differentiating it yields the negative variance. Every \(\pi _j\) is positive, so that variance vanishes exactly when all component exponents agree. Applying the secant identity to \(-\log A(e^x)\) bounds the regression by its extreme derivatives. An exact power would have constant local slope.

💡 In plain words

When two power profiles are added, the logarithm of the sum usually curves. The derivative of its local slope is minus a variance; hence a mixture with different exponents can look like a distance-dependent exponent without either component changing its law.

Constant finite normalizers can be absorbed in \(a_j\). Changing the heads, their weights or their supports with distance can violate the hypotheses. This log-sum-exp identity does not establish that individual heads are powers or identify their computational roles.

K.4 Group 4: ordering discrete mass quantiles

Theorem K.4 Exponent and support order
#
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

Let \(N\ge 2\) be an integer and \(p_g(d)=d^{-g}/Z_N(g)\) on \(\{ 1,\ldots ,N\} \), with \(g\in \mathbb R\). For \(1\le k{\lt}N\), the prefix mass \(F_g(k)=\sum _{d\le k}p_g(d)\) is strictly increasing in \(g\). For \(0{\lt}f{\lt}1\), the well-defined integer quantile

\[ D_f(g,N)=\min \{ k\in \{ 1,\ldots ,N\} :F_g(k)\ge f\} \]

is nonincreasing in \(g\) and, for fixed \(g,f\), nondecreasing in \(N\). These conclusions include negative exponents, zero and one.

Isabelle · ours · partshow

Only a part is in Isabelle: The minimum that defines the quantile is taken over non-empty finite sets.

  shows "quantile h fract\<le>quantile g fract"

  assumes N: "1\<le>N" and NM: "N\<le>M" and fn: "fract\<le>F N" and gm: "fract\<le>G M"
    and order: "\<And>k. k\<in>{1..N} \<Longrightarrow> G k\<le>F k"
  shows "finite_quantile N F fract\<le>finite_quantile M G fract"

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: part: The minimum that defines the quantile is taken over non-empty finite sets.·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

The defining set is finite and contains \(N\). Put \(X=\log d\) and \(L_k=\{ 1,\ldots ,k\} \). Differentiating the finite sums gives

\[ \partial _gF_g(k)=-\operatorname {Cov}_{p_g}({\bf 1}_{L_k},X) =P(L_k)P(L_k^c) \big({\mathbb {E}}[X\mid L_k^c]-{\mathbb {E}}[X\mid L_k]\big){\gt}0. \]

Both groups have positive mass and every logarithm in the second exceeds every logarithm in the first. Increasing \(g\) can only advance the first crossing of \(f\). Increasing \(N\) leaves an old prefix numerator unchanged and increases its denominator; it cannot produce an earlier crossing.

💡 In plain words

With fixed support, increasing the exponent shifts mass toward short distances, so the quantile cannot increase. Enlarging the support can move it in the opposite direction. These are finite orderings under the stated conditions, not an automatic recipe for choosing a KV window.

The integer quantile is a step function, so its monotonicity need not be strict. This family property supplies a mass budget, not a KV task guarantee.

K.5 Group 5: finite-family calculus and sensitivity

Theorem K.5✅ Isabelle Smoothness, entropy and divergence bounds
#
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

For integer \(N\ge 1\) and real \(g,h\), let \(\psi (g)=\log Z_N(g)\), \(U(g)={\mathbb {E}}_{p_g}\log d\), \(I(g)=\operatorname {Var}_{p_g}(\log d)\) and \(S(g)=-\sum _dp_g(d)\log p_g(d)\). All these functions are smooth to every order for finite \(g\), and

\[ \psi '=-U,\quad \psi ''=I,\quad U'=-I,\quad S=\psi +gU,\quad S'=-gI,\quad C_V=g^2I. \]

Writing \(L=\log N\),

\[ 0\le I(g)\le L^2/4,\qquad 0\le C_V(g)\le g^2L^2/4. \]

Moreover,

\begin{align} \operatorname {KL}(p_g\Vert p_h) & =(h-g)U(g)+\psi (h)-\psi (g)\notag \\ & =(h-g)^2\int _0^1(1-t)I(g+t(h-g))\, dt\notag \\ & \le (h-g)^2L^2/8,\\ \operatorname {TV}(p_g,p_h) & \le \tanh \! \left(\frac{|h-g|L}{4}\right) \le \min \{ 1,|h-g|L/4\} . \end{align}

For \(N\ge 2\), \(I(g){\gt}0\), and \(S\) has its unique maximum at \(g=0\).

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: the whole statement·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

🆕 Classical and new: Classical identities of finite exponential families, applied here to attention profiles.

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

Differentiate the finite sums using \(p_g'=-p_g(\log d-U)\). Positivity of \(Z_N\) makes its logarithm and all quotients smooth. For \(X\in [0,L]\), \({\mathbb {E}}[X(L-X)]\ge 0\) yields \(\operatorname {Var}X\le L{\mathbb {E}}X-({\mathbb {E}}X)^2\le L^2/4\). The log-ratio of probabilities gives the KL identity. Taylor’s integral remainder for \(\psi \) gives the next equality, also for \(h{\lt}g\); integrating the variance bound gives \(L^2(h-g)^2/8\). The two power distributions are softmaxes whose score difference has oscillation \(|h-g|L\). Group 7 proves the TV bound, and \(\tanh u\le \min \{ 1,u\} \) for \(u\ge 0\) gives its linear form. For \(N\ge 2\) at least two distinct log-distances have positive mass; thus \(I{\gt}0\) and \(S'=-gI\) proves the unique maximum. For \(N=1\) all displayed quantities and divergences are zero.

💡 In plain words

A partition function generates the mean, the variance and the derivatives of this finite family. The KL divergence between two parameters is exactly a convex remainder. For finite support there is no mathematical singularity at parameter one; the identities are standard for exponential families.

One generating function, with a base-measure qualification.

More generally, for positive fixed weights \(a_j\) and real energies \(E_j\), \(\psi (t)=\log \sum _ja_je^{-tE_j}\) gives \(-\psi '={\mathbb {E}}_tE\) and \(\psi ''=\operatorname {Var}_t(E)\). Groups 3 and 5 are instances with energies \(g_j\) and \(\log d\), respectively. The Shannon identity \(S=\psi +tU\) used above assumes unit base weights; with arbitrary \(a_j\) it includes the extra term \(-{\mathbb {E}}_t\log a_j\). At finite support, \(g=1\) is not a singularity. The continuous value \((\log N)^2/12\) at one is not substituted for the discrete variance.

K.6 Group 6: what renormalized row truncation guarantees

Theorem K.6 Exact divergences and sharp frozen-output bounds
#
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

Let \(p\) be a probability on a finite nonempty key set and retain a subset \(K\) with \(p(K)=1-\epsilon {\gt}0\). Set \(q_j=p_j/(1-\epsilon )\) in \(K\) and \(q_j=0\) outside. Then

\[ \operatorname {TV}(p,q)=\epsilon ,\qquad \operatorname {KL}(q\Vert p)=-\log (1-\epsilon ). \]

If \(\epsilon {\gt}0\), then \(\operatorname {KL}(p\Vert q)=+\infty \). For fixed values \(v_j\), \(o=\sum _jp_jv_j\) and \(o_K=\sum _jq_jv_j\) satisfy

\begin{equation} \| o-o_K\| \le \epsilon \operatorname {diam}\{ v_j\} \le 2\epsilon \max _j\| v_j\| . \end{equation}
103

For \(\epsilon {\gt}0\), if \(o_R\) is the conditional mean over removed keys, \(o-o_K=\epsilon (o_R-o_K)\). The constants one and two are optimal in general.

Isabelle · ours · partshow

Only a part is in Isabelle: A network that changes after truncation requires separate evaluation.

truncation_tv · Isabelle/TransformerAttentionPartI/TAF_Truncation.thy, line 43 — total variation equals the removed mass

lemma truncation_tv: "tv_distance S p (cut_prob K p) = 1-sum p K"

frozen_output_exact · Isabelle/TransformerAttentionPartI/TAF_Vector_Output.thy, line 89 — exact output difference for a frozen row

lemma frozen_output_exact:
  assumes "sum p K<1"
  shows "norm (vector_mean S p v-vector_mean S (cut_prob K p) v) =
    (1-sum p K)*norm (vector_mean S (cut_prob (S-K) p) v-vector_mean S (cut_prob K p) v)"

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: part: A network that changes after truncation requires separate evaluation.·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

In \(K\), the nonnegative differences \(q_j-p_j\) sum to \(\epsilon \); outside, the \(p_j\) also sum to \(\epsilon \). This proves TV. On the positive support of \(q\), its likelihood ratio to \(p\) is \(1/(1-\epsilon )\), giving reverse KL. Positive removed mass creates a positive \(p_j\) with \(q_j=0\), giving infinite forward KL. For \(\epsilon {\gt}0\), decompose \(o=(1-\epsilon )o_K+\epsilon o_R\). The difference of the two conditional means is a convex combination of differences \(v_r-v_k\) and is bounded by the diameter, which is at most twice the maximum norm. For \(\epsilon =0\) the two distributions and outputs agree. A retained value \(-Bu\) and a removed value \(Bu\), with \(\| u\| =1\), \(B{\gt}0\) and masses \(1-\epsilon ,\epsilon \), attain both bounds.

💡 In plain words

If mass \(\varepsilon \) is removed from a row and the rest is renormalized, its total-variation distance from the original is exactly \(\varepsilon \). The output difference also decomposes exactly into the removed mean and the retained one. This assumes a frozen row.

The scores and values are frozen. A subsequent linear projection contributes its operator norm; propagation through a changing network needs additional stability assumptions. No perplexity or answer-quality guarantee follows alone.

K.7 Group 7: from score errors to softmax errors

Theorem K.7✅ Isabelle Sharp oscillation stability
#
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

On a finite nonempty support, let \(q=\operatorname {softmax}(s)\) and \(p=\operatorname {softmax}(s+r)\) for finite real scores. With \(\omega =\max _jr_j-\min _jr_j\),

\begin{equation} \operatorname {TV}(p,q)\le \tanh (\omega /4). \end{equation}
104

The bound is optimal over positive distributions and errors with this oscillation. If \(|r_j|\le \eta \), then TV is at most \(\tanh (\eta /2)\). For fixed values,

\[ \left\| \sum _j(p_j-q_j)v_j\right\| \le \operatorname {diam}\{ v_j\} \tanh (\omega /4). \]
Isabelle · oursshow

    and lo: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> l \<le> r i"
    and hi: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> r i \<le> u"
  shows "tv_distance S (finite_softmax S s) (finite_softmax S (\<lambda>i. s i+r i))
    \<le> tanh ((u-l)/4)"

logarithmic_score_stability · Isabelle/TransformerAttentionPartI/TAF_Log_Scores.thy, line 40 — stability from logarithmic scores

lemma logarithmic_score_stability:
  assumes fin: "finite S" and ne: "S\<noteq>{}"
    and pos: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> 0<d i"
    and lo: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> l\<le>r i"
    and hi: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> r i\<le>u"
  shows "tv_distance S (finite_power_profile S d g)
      (finite_softmax S (\<lambda>i. b-g*ln (d i)+r i))\<le>tanh ((u-l)/4)"

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: the whole statement·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Used in: Theorem K.8

Proof ▼

A constant score shift cancels, proving the case \(\omega =0\). Otherwise shift the errors so that \(Y_j=e^{r_j}\in [1,M]\), \(M=e^\omega {\gt}1\), and let \(\mu ={\mathbb {E}}_qY\). Then \(p_j=q_jY_j/\mu \), so \(\operatorname {TV}(p,q)={\mathbb {E}}_q|Y-\mu |/(2\mu )\). The chord of the convex function \(|y-\mu |\) on \([1,M]\) gives

\[ \operatorname {TV}(p,q)\le \frac{(\mu -1)(M-\mu )}{\mu (M-1)} \le \frac{\sqrt M-1}{\sqrt M+1}=\tanh (\omega /4). \]

The second inequality follows from \((\mu -\sqrt M)^2\ge 0\). Equality is attained with \(Y=1,M\) and respective probabilities \(\sqrt M/(1+\sqrt M)\) and \(1/(1+\sqrt M)\), which give \(\mu =\sqrt M\). These strictly positive probabilities are realized by finite softmax scores. The absolute error bound gives \(\omega \le 2\eta \). Finally the positive and negative parts of \(p-q\) each have mass TV; normalizing them expresses the output difference as TV times a difference of convex combinations, bounded by the diameter. If TV is zero the output difference is zero directly.

💡 In plain words

Attention changes only if the differences between scores change: adding the same constant to all of them has no effect. A sharp total-variation bound depends on the oscillation of the error. The precision of the result depends on bounding that oscillation for the actual scores.

🧪 Lab: Sharp softmax stability for your score errors

Compare two finite softmax rows and the sharp total-variation bound from score-error oscillation.

Logarithmic-score corollary.

If scores on a declared finite nonempty set of positive distances are \(s_d=b-g\log d+r_d\), their row distribution is within \(\tanh ((\max r-\min r)/4)\) in TV of \(d^{-g}/\sum _{u\in \mathcal D}u^{-g}\) on that same support. A constant remainder gives exact equality. This follows by applying the theorem to the unperturbed scores \(b-g\log d\). The hypothesis concerns individual row scores. A statement about mean scores does not allow interchange of expectation and softmax.

K.8 Group 8: a cosine integral with an explicit RoPE remainder

Theorem K.8 Cosine-grid approximation and logarithmic remainder
#

Uses

  • Theorem K.7
  • Theorem K.7
📍 map❝ cite⚠ report

For integer \(m\ge 1\), \(\theta {\gt}1\), \(L=\log \theta \) and real \(d{\gt}0\), define

\[ S_m(d)=\sum _{i=0}^{m-1}\cos (d\theta ^{-i/m}),\qquad J_m(d)=\frac{m}{L}\big[\operatorname {Ci}(d)-\operatorname {Ci}(d/\theta )\big], \]

where \(\operatorname {Ci}(x)=-\int _x^\infty \cos t/t\, dt\) for \(x{\gt}0\). Then

\begin{align} |S_m(d)-J_m(d)|& \le \int _{d/\theta }^{d}|\sin u|\, du \le d(1-1/\theta ),\\ \left|S_m(d)-\frac{m}{L}(L-\gamma _E-\log d)\right| & \le B_m(d),\\ B_m(d)& =d(1-1/\theta )+\frac{m}{L} \left(\frac2d+\frac{d^2}{4\theta ^2}\right),\notag \end{align}

with Euler’s constant \(\gamma _E\). At fixed \(d,\theta \), the normalized Riemann approximation has error at most \(d(1-1/\theta )/m\), tending to zero as \(m\to \infty \).

  assumes m: "0<m" and theta: "1<theta" and d: "0<d"
  shows "abs (rope_cosine_sum m theta d-real m/ln theta*(ln theta-euler_mascheroni-ln d))

lemma conditional_rope_power_row:
  fixes a c :: real
  assumes fin: "finite S" and ne: "S\<noteq>{}"
    and m: "0<m" and theta: "1<theta" and h: "0<h"
    and d: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> 0<d i"
    and B: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> rope_logarithmic_error_bound m theta (d i)\<le>B"
    and e: "\<And>i. i\<in>S \<Longrightarrow> abs (e i)\<le>rho"
  defines "g \<equiv> a*real m/(sqrt h*ln theta)"
    and "eta \<equiv> abs a*B/sqrt h+rho"
  shows "tv_distance S (finite_power_profile S d g)
      (finite_softmax S (\<lambda>i. c+a*rope_cosine_sum m theta (d i)/sqrt h+e i))\<le>tanh (eta/2)"

Proof: in this note·Formalized: Isabelle/HOL, by the author (public formalizations repository)·Covers: part: The hypothesis on scores is not derived from the architecture or from training.·Cite: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24379538

↳ Not used by another result of the paper.

Proof ▼

Set \(f(t)=\cos (de^{-Lt})\). Substitution gives \(m\int _0^1f(t)\, dt=J_m(d)\). On each cell \(I_i=[i/m,(i+1)/m]\),

\[ \left|f(i/m)-m\int _{I_i}f(t)\, dt\right| \le m\int _{I_i}\int _{i/m}^t|f'(u)|\, du\, dt \le \int _{I_i}|f'(u)|\, du. \]

Summing and changing variables proves the absolute-sine bound. Integration by parts in the tail integral gives \(|\operatorname {Ci}(d)|\le 2/d\). The standard Euler normalization is

\[ \operatorname {Ci}(y)=\gamma _E+\log y+ \int _0^y\frac{\cos t-1}{t}\, dt. \]

The inequality \(|1-\cos t|\le t^2/2\) bounds the last integral in magnitude by \(y^2/4\). Apply these bounds at \(d\) and \(y=d/\theta \), multiply by \(m/L\), and add the Riemann error. Dividing Equation (95) by \(m\) proves the normalized convergence. The formal development also establishes the link to the Euler-normalized special function, rather than assuming an unspecified integration constant.

💡 In plain words

The cosine sum over RoPE planes is compared with an integral on a logarithmic scale; the cosine integral function gives an exact representation and an explicit remainder. The subsequent step to a softmax row requires a separate hypothesis on the scores. The bound may be too large for a useful approximation.

Conditional transfer to an attention row.

Let \(h{\gt}0\), \(a,c\in \mathbb R\), \(\rho \ge 0\) and retain the theorem’s conditions. On a finite nonempty support of positive distances, suppose the actual row scores satisfy \(s_d=c+aS_m(d)/\sqrt h+e_d\), \(|e_d|\le \rho \). Set

\begin{equation} g=\frac{am}{\sqrt h\log \theta },\qquad \eta =\frac{|a|}{\sqrt h}\max _{d\in \mathcal D}B_m(d)+\rho . \tag {97} \end{equation}
107

Their softmax is within \(\tanh (\eta /2)\) in TV of the power family of exponent \(g\) on the same support. Indeed the score is \(b-g\log d+r_d\), where \(b=c+g(L-\gamma _E)\) and \(|r_d|\le \eta \); Group 7 applies. The finite nonempty support makes the maximum valid.

Equivalently, put

\[ \delta _m(d)=\frac{L}{m}B_m(d) =\frac{Ld}{m}(1-1/\theta )+\frac2d+\frac14(d/\theta )^2. \]

Then \(\eta =|g|\max _d\delta _m(d)+\rho \). The three terms separate discretization, small-distance and large-relative-distance errors. The bound can be large and uninformative. Normalized convergence to the cosine integral does not eliminate its logarithmic-approximation error. Unequal plane amplitudes, sine components, unrotated coordinates and content dependence must satisfy the score hypothesis or be controlled in \(e_d\). The self-distance \(d=0\) is outside this logarithmic support and must be treated separately if included in a full attention row. No formula for \(\gamma _P(\theta ,T)\) or learned exponent follows without further premises.

For reproduction with Isabelle2026 and AFP 2026-11-06 installed, run isabelle build with one job, one thread, quick-and-dirty disabled, the AFP theories as a session directory, and the supplied snapshot as the session to build. The exact command and dependency provenance are provided in the source-package instructions.

The written proofs and formal objects establish the stated finite-family, instrument and approximation results. They do not certify all claims in the manuscript, bibliographic novelty, missing empirical provenance, uniqueness of a heat-capacity maximum for every support size, learned circuit labels, or task quality after interventions. The historical 20-lemma audit in Appendix A remains a separate record with its original scope.

Table 35. Revised interpretation of diagnostic observations. None of these observations alone licenses pruning or model selection.
ObservationFollow-up
Poor power-law fitInspect support, masks, sinks and competing families; do not infer architecture from $R^2$.
Fit near or above oneCompute finite-support quantities; validate any cache policy with task outcomes.
Nonzero corpus contrastPreserve both estimates and their uncertainty; check matched metadata and corpus-load success.
Head or layer heterogeneityInspect individual profiles; establish circuit function with direct tests.
Large mass quantileTreat as a distributional calculation, not a guarantee of useful retained context.

Table 41. Corrected failure atlas. Empirical reports and mathematical limitations have different evidential status.
TopicObservation and implication
Near $g=1$The sub-one large-$N$ approximation tends to zero at fixed $N$; the finite continuous quantile instead tends to $N^f$. The discrete normalizer is finite. Use the appropriate finite-support calculation.
$g>1$Both finite quantiles remain defined. A Phase-A asymptotic approximation is inappropriate; measured cache performance is still a separate outcome.
Base/instructEight rounded D3 pairs have two increases, three decreases and three small changes. Missing raw output prevents a full replay or causal RLHF claim.
GQA ratioObserved signs do not follow the proposed monotone gate. Mixed models and a chosen singular reference do not identify a causal mechanism.
ALiBiA reported numerical zero at 5000 does not uniquely identify exponential collapse. Inspect masks, content and precision before interpreting it.
Mittag–LefflerThe reported median ratio $.23$ uses a different denominator from the $1.30$ power-family comparison. Each exact-normalization ratio would target one; neither establishes a waiting-time process.
Tanh trajectoryThe historical four-checkpoint $R^2=.15$ and nonmonotone slopes do not support the tested monotone trajectory, or identify a hidden time axis.
Coordinate pruningDescriptive costs do not validate a rotary-band boundary; the inspected masks include non-rotary coordinates. Absence of a step does not prove absence of all causal hubs.
Polymer analogy$3g/(1+2g)$ is an untested substitution, not a measured spreading exponent. No dynamical polymer interpretation is established.
Adaptive controllersWhole-sequence gates fail prefix causality. Their saved teacher-forced scores do not certify causal autoregressive perplexity.
Möbius clusterAll 23 configurations lie outside the test radius on the horizontal axis alone; the observed zero is structurally forced.

ModeIntended function and necessary qualification
ProfileCollect metadata, formulas and recorded profiles; distinguish measured and predicted fields.
UnmaskInspect position/scaling settings; configuration limits do not measure practical context quality.

LongScorePresent stored long-context comparisons; retain benchmark versions and protocols rather than certify current rankings.

JSON CoTFlag output-field order; schema order alone does not prove or disprove reasoning quality.
PEFT LintInspect scripts for known patterns; static checks cannot establish a successful training run.
Cache DiffEstimate provider-specific cache effects using explicit current rules and measured hits.
Spec-DecodeCompare tokenizers; mismatch is a compatibility concern, not proof that every method is slower than baseline.

$S_N$$g,N$Shannon distance entropy; asymptotics require a specified fixed-$g$ regime.

Table 46. Formula catalogue with support and interpretation stated explicitly.
ObjectExpressionScope
Finite family$p_\gamma(d)=d^{-\gamma}/Z_N$, $Z_N=\sum_{d=1}^N d^{-\gamma}$Integer $N\ge1$, real $\gamma$, counting measure.
Log moment$U_N=\sum_d p_\gamma(d)\log d$Equals $-\partial_\gamma\log Z_N$.
Entropy$S_N=\log Z_N+\gamma U_N$Exact finite-sum Shannon entropy; $0\le S_N\le\log N$.
Fisher metric$I(\gamma)=\operatorname{Var}_{p_\gamma}(\log d)$Finite at every real $\gamma$ for fixed $N$; evaluate directly at zero.
Formal heat capacity$C_V=\gamma^2I(\gamma)$Family susceptibility, not an identified task sensitivity.
Intrinsic length$\left|\int_{g_1}^{g_2}\sqrt{I(g)}\,dg\right|$Distance along this statistical family.
Continuous normalizer$Z_c=(N^{1-\gamma}-1)/(1-\gamma)$; $Z_c(1)=\log N$Lebesgue measure on $[1,N]$, $N>1$; not the discrete normalizer.
Variance at one$C_{V,c}(1)=(\log N)^2/12$Continuous only. For discrete distances use the variance of $\log d$.
Free-energy coordinate$-\log Z_N$Dimensionless coordinate; division by $\gamma$ gives the thermal convention for $\gamma\ne0$.
Discrete mass window$\min\{k:\sum_{d=1}^k d^{-\gamma}\ge fZ_N\}$Integer distance quantile; $0<f<1$.
Continuous mass window$[(1-f)+fN^{1-\gamma}]^{1/(1-\gamma)}$; $N^f$ at $\gamma=1$Quantile of the continuous family, not an accuracy bound.
Padé candidate$(2\theta-T\sqrt2)/(2\theta+T\sqrt2)$$\theta,T>0$; range $(-1,1)$; empirical identification unestablished.
Inverse base$T\sqrt2(1+g)/(2(1-g))$$-1<g<1$, $T>0$; candidate inversion, not a task optimum.
Inverse context$d_{\rm inv}=\theta\sqrt2(1-g)/(1+g)$$-1<g<1$, $\theta>0$; not a validated retrieval ceiling.
Shifted base$b(T)=\theta+T/\sqrt2$Exact coordinate definition; different from the inverse base.
Log base ratio$\log[b(D)/b(N)]$Signed coordinate change, not established information loss.
Threshold exponent$d_{\rm eff}=1/\gamma$, $\gamma>0$Records a weight-threshold count exponent, not measured geometric dimension.
Effective support$\exp S_N$Entropy effective number within the chosen family, not a task context limit.
Frozen-row bound$\|o-o_K\|\le\epsilon\,\operatorname{diam}\{v_j\}$Fixed scores and values, renormalized retained row, removed mass $0\le\epsilon<1$.
Soft decay$w(d)=(1-d/d_{\rm inv})^\gamma$ inside $0<d<d_{\rm inv}$For positive $\gamma,d_{\rm inv}$: use $\log w$ as a score bias; an empirical proposal, not a geometry theorem.
Corpus contrast$\widehat\gamma_{\rm random}-\widehat\gamma_{\rm text}$Matched-protocol descriptive statistic; not a causal architecture identifier.

Table 49. Current status of F1–F20. Retained empirical observations are not new replications.
IDOriginal topicCurrent conclusionLocation
F1Padé predictorAlgebraic candidate. Universal derivation withdrawn; initial and October panels have different protocols and denominators.§5.3
F2Rotary geometryExact cycle counts require the actual rotary subspace and pairing convention. Completing a cycle does not prove loss of information.§4.2
F3Boundary at oneInfinite-support summability boundary. Finite sums are analytic; $(\log N)^2/12$ is the continuous variance, not the discrete value.§7
F4Entropy lawFinite entropy bound and distinct fixed-exponent asymptotics. The old leading factor $(1-\gamma)$ is incorrect.§7.4
F5Semantic reservoirUnsupported by the inspected masks: B3 removes unequal coordinate sets; the amplification script also changes V.§13
F6Band dissociationFull B3 sweep retained. The larger coordinate mask has higher PPL in all six windows; no semantic/positional double dissociation.§7.4
F7KV windowExact discrete and continuous mass quantiles are different. Recorded truncation trials do not establish a universal accuracy-preserving range.§11
F8NTK scalingBase multiplier differs from context factor. B1 ratios hid short-context PPL costs; candidate-ranking counts do not establish Pareto dominance or a universal optimum.§12
F9Base designCorrected table generated from the inverse equation. At $T=4096$, targets $0.5$ and $0.85$ give about 8689 and 35721; task assignments are unvalidated.§12.1
F10GQA pressureArchitectural association hypothesis. Mixed configurations and corpora do not isolate a causal effect of the number of KV heads.§8.4
F11Boiling criterionThresholds for forgetting or loss spikes are unvalidated. A family heat capacity is not a measured risk probability.§7.2
F12Induction thresholdA universal sign transition near 400M parameters is unsupported; fitting supports and alternative mechanisms matter.§8.4
F13SWA confinementMasking affects available keys, but the reported cross-model contrasts do not identify a universal exponent shift.§16
F14Alignment shiftsHistorical base/instruction pairs retain their measured differences. They do not isolate RLHF from SFT, DPO or other changes.§15
F15HolographyA Shannon entropy bound does not establish entanglement geometry, a Ryu–Takayanagi identification or universal central charge.§7.4
F16Fisher identity$C_V=\gamma^2I$ is exact in the finite family. Division by $\gamma^2$ excludes zero, and extrema need not coincide.§7.3
F17RG flowThe rational-coordinate differential equation and its solution are conditional algebra, not a measured training trajectory.§20.2
F18Controller recoveryAdaptive historical hooks pool future positions and fail prefix causality; their scores do not certify causal PPL. Recovery denominators differ and the Fisher prediction is withdrawn. November tests are separate evidence.§19.2
F19Soft decayRecorded policy comparisons remain protocol-specific. The score bias is $\log w(d)$, not $w(d)$; no general PPL improvement follows.§11.6
F20Pruning costSlopes on two model experiments are descriptive fits, not a universal cost law or a cross-model uncertainty interval. The proposed layer cutoff was withdrawn.App. F

Table 50. Resolution of identified errors. Implementation checks do not create missing historical observations.
IDIssueResolution in this edition
1Geometric prediction of trained attentionScore decomposition retained; missing statistical premises made explicit. Configuration-only universality and the invalid derivation are withdrawn. Sections 5.2–5.4.
2Variable-length measurement confoundThe E4 and field nulls use their actual protocols. Fixed-query QL is distinguished, with provenance and missing observations stated. Sections 9.1 and 14.3.
3Finite and continuous thermodynamicsSeparate normalizers, moments, Fisher information and quantiles; correct domains and finite value at one. Sections 6.4–7.4.
4KV performance guaranteesExact mass budgets and frozen-row bounds replace configuration-only accuracy claims; experimental policies and denominators remain distinct. Section 11.
5Rotary/semantic band interpretationActual rotary subspace, pairing and adjacent-coordinate masks are reported. Coordinate ablations no longer identify semantic frequency bands. Sections 11.7 and 13.
6Inverse base and NIAH guaranteesCorrect inverse and explicit test protocols; algebraic identities are not independent retrieval predictions. Section 12.
7Corpus, lexical and architecture labelsMatched observables and missing query/count records are stated. Signs do not identify induction heads, SWA or GQA. Sections 14.3–16.
8Control uses future positionsNew per-query reference passes prefix and partition checks. Defective historical scores are not relabelled as causal PPL. Section 19.3.
9Wrong head-projection boundaryNew reference acts before the inspected NeoX mixing projection, with declared layout checks. Post-projection blocks are not called heads. Section 19.3.
10Non-unit, incorrectly paired rotationsNew tables use unique frequencies and explicit pairing; norm, inverse rotation and unrotated-tail checks pass. Section 19.3.
11Controller summaries and denominatorsAll saved rows retained; recovery denominators and layer comparisons corrected. No Fisher-based efficacy claim. Section 19.2.
12Potential, stability and finite-time claimCorrect potential and exact trajectory; positive endpoint repels and negative endpoint attracts in the stated direction. Section 20.2.
13Möbius domain and fixed-point testRight-half-plane mapping and determinant corrected; 0/23 clustering is structurally uninformative. Section 20.3.
14Fractional/CFT/BTZ identificationsCorrect algebra and domain conditions; unsupported physical equivalences withdrawn. Section 20.
15Complete-proof and Taylor claimsInvalid averaging and normalization steps removed; inverse compositions and numerical errors corrected. Appendix B.
16Zipf, grokking, signs and rangesComplete saved panels, proper correlation domains and actual probe support replace the earlier summaries. Appendices D and F.
17V1/V2 context-input mismatchOld panel rejected as validation; replacement interface requires an independently declared token context. Explicit illustrative calculations are provided in Appendix F.
18Catalogue, software and glossaryCorrect counts, calculation domains and terminology; obsolete verdict screenshot replaced by an evaluation workflow. Section 21 and Appendix I.
19Alpha-S products and circuit labelsProducts recomputed from declared inputs. Classification marks and unsupported training-budget decisions removed. Appendix H.
20Bibliographic errorsIncorrect locators, titles and authors corrected; blogs identified; version-sensitive citation pinned; argumentative notes removed. Source metadata and exact changes are archived.
21Contradictory archival prose and notationErroneous prose moved to the separate predecessor archive. $d_{\rm head}$ and $d_{\rm inv}$ now denote distinct objects throughout.
